Use protected branches, mandatory reviews, separation of duties author cannot be the only approver and approval gates on production environments, while the pipeline records the evidence automatically: who approved, what artifact digest, which scans and tests passed.

title: Untrusted pipeline
text: How do you restore trust in the pipeline? Your 30-engineer team's CI pipeline now fails about 35% of runs for reasons unrelated to the change. Engineers click "re-run" until it is green. Pipeline time is 28 minutes. Last month a real regression merged because its failure was assumed to be "just flaky".

title: Contract testing
text: What is consumer-driven contract testing and why use it instead of end-to-end tests between services? The consumer records the requests it makes and the responses it expects as a contract; the provider's pipeline replays those contracts to prove it still satisfies every consumer. A broker stores contracts and a can-i-deploy check gates releases. It is faster and less brittle than end-to-end tests and lets teams deploy independently.

title: Load testing
text: How do you include performance testing in a CI/CD pipeline? A short smoke load test with thresholds for example p95 under 300 ms, errors under 1% on each merge to staging, and a full load, stress and soak test nightly or before big launches in a production-like environment, compared against a baseline. Use realistic data and traffic mix, warm caches, and watch system metrics such as CPU, DB and queue depth.

title: Preview environments
text: Why use ephemeral per-PR environments instead of one shared staging environment? A shared staging mixes everyone's changes, queues testers and produces flakiness. An ephemeral environment gives each PR its own full stack and URL for review and testing and is destroyed on merge or after a TTL, so tests are isolated and parallel. Costs are controlled with TTLs and scale-to-zero.

title: Dependencies
text: How do you manage third-party dependencies safely and keep them up to date? Use lockfiles and pinned versions for reproducible builds, automate update PRs with Dependabot or Renovate so each runs the full CI, alert on vulnerabilities with a fix SLA, mirror registries, and watch for typosquatting and dependency confusion by using scoped names and registry rules.

title: Supply chain
text: What are an SBOM, artifact signing and SLSA provenance, and how do they defend the supply chain? An SBOM lists every component in an artifact so you can instantly find where a vulnerable library is used. Signing Sigstore/cosign proves an artifact came from your pipeline and verification at deploy time rejects anything else. SLSA provenance attests how, where and from what source an artifact was built, with higher levels requiring tamper-resistant builds.

title: Risky workflow change
text: What is wrong, and how do you prevent this class of mistake? A contributor opens a PR that modifies .github/workflows/ci.yml to use pull request target and check out the PR head so that PRs from forks get "faster previews". The diff is 6 lines and a teammate has approved it as "tiny".

title: Three signals
text: What are metrics, logs and traces, and when do you use each? Metrics are numbers over time and tell you something is wrong. Traces follow one request across services and tell you where. Logs are detailed event records and tell you why. A correlation or trace ID ties them together, and OpenTelemetry is the vendor-neutral standard for emitting all three.

title: SLO and error budget
text: Explain SLI, SLO, SLA and error budget. How does an error budget influence releases? An SLI is a measurement, such as the percentage of requests that succeed under 300 ms. An SLO is the target, say 99.9% over 30 days. An SLA is the contractual promise with penalties, usually looser. The error budget is 100% minus the SLO, about 43 minutes per 30 days at 99.9%. If the budget is nearly spent, slow down risky releases and invest in reliability; if plenty remains, ship faster.

title: Alerting
text: What makes a good alert, and how do you avoid alert fatigue? A good alert is actionable, urgent and based on user-visible symptoms, and links to a runbook. Page humans only when users are affected now; send the rest to tickets or dashboards. Replace many noisy resource alerts with a few SLO burn-rate alerts, and review alerts regularly, deleting those that nobody acts on.

title: DORA metrics
text: What are the four DORA metrics and how would you improve each? Deployment frequency and lead time for changes measure speed; change failure rate and time to restore measure stability. Improve frequency and lead time with smaller PRs, faster CI, automated deploys and flags. Reduce failure rate with better tests, canaries and gates. Reduce restore time with fast rollback, good alerts and runbooks.

title: Incident response
text: A deployment may have caused an outage. What is your first move and why? Mitigate first, diagnose later. If a recent change is the likely cause, roll back or turn off the flag immediately, because that is usually the fastest way to end user impact. Then confirm recovery on the SLIs, communicate, and investigate calmly, finishing with a blameless post-mortem.

title: Noisy on-call
text: How do you fix the on-call situation? Your team of 8 is paged about 60 times a week, mostly CPU and memory threshold alerts that auto-resolve. Two engineers have threatened to leave the rotation. Last Tuesday a real checkout outage was acknowledged late because the page looked like the usual noise. Users saw errors for 22 minutes.

title: Prometheus
text: Explain Prometheus metric types and why high-cardinality labels are dangerous. Counters only go up use rate on them , gauges go up and down, histograms record distributions for percentiles. Prometheus scrapes endpoints and stores a separate time series for every unique label combination, so a label such as user id creates millions of series and can exhaust memory and crash the server. Keep labels bounded.

title: Logging
text: How should an application log in a containerised environment? Write structured JSON logs to stdout with timestamp, level, service, version and a trace or request ID. A node agent Fluent Bit, Vector, Promtail ships them to a store such as Loki or Elasticsearch. Control cost with sampling and retention tiers, and never log secrets or personal data.

title: Tracing
text: What is distributed tracing and what is OpenTelemetry? A trace follows one request across services as a tree of spans linked by a trace ID propagated in headers W3C traceparent , showing where time is spent. OpenTelemetry is the vendor-neutral standard with SDKs and a Collector that receives, samples and exports telemetry to backends such as Jaeger, Tempo or Datadog.

title: Dashboards
text: What makes a good service dashboard during an incident? Organised by questions: is it healthy golden signals and SLO status , what changed deploy and flag markers , and where is the problem split by version, region, endpoint and dependency . A small top-level health view with drill-downs, not a wall of graphs, and a canary versus baseline panel during rollouts.

title: Synthetic and RUM
text: What is the difference between synthetic monitoring and real user monitoring, and why use both? Synthetic monitoring runs scripted probes of key journeys from several regions on a schedule, detecting outages even with no traffic and checking DNS, TLS and CDN. RUM collects performance and errors from real browsers and apps, showing real experience across devices and networks. Synthetic gives controlled consistency; RUM gives truth.

title: Capacity and cost
text: How do you keep observability costs under control, and how do you do capacity planning? Control cardinality, drop unused metrics, sample traces and noisy logs, aggregate before storing and use retention tiers. For capacity, trend utilisation CPU, memory, disk, connections, queue depth , forecast time to saturation, load test to find limits, and plan peak headroom of 30-50% with autoscaling.

title: Post-mortem
text: How would you rewrite this post-mortem? A junior engineer ran a cleanup script against production instead of staging and deleted 40 minutes of order data before the backup restore completed. The draft post-mortem says "root cause: engineer error" and proposes "be more careful".

title: Identity vs equality
text: What is the difference between a class and an object, and between == and equals in Java? A class is the blueprint, an object is one heap instance built from it. A variable holds a reference, so == asks "same object?" while equals asks "same meaning?". If I override equals I must override hashCode too, or HashMap and HashSet break.

title: Encapsulation of state
text: What is wrong, and how would you restructure the class? A teammate's order code has been live for a month. Support reports orders stuck in status PADI and one empty order that was paid. class Order { public long id; public List<String items = new ArrayList< ; public String status; } // scattered over 6 files order.items.add "shoes" ; order.status = "PADI"; if order.items.size == 0 { / forgot to block empty checkout / }

title: Construction order
text: In what order do static initialisers, field initialisers, instance blocks and constructors run, and why is calling an overridable method from a constructor dangerous? Static init runs once at class load. Per new , the parent finishes first fields, then constructor body , then the child's fields, then the child's constructor. If the parent constructor calls an overridable method, the child's override runs before the child's fields are set, so it sees nulls and zeros.

title: Static state
text: Explain both symptoms and fix them. A service counts created orders for a dashboard. 8 request threads, 1,000,000 creations in a load test, the counter shows 712,340. class OrderIdGenerator { static int created; static int next { created++; return created; } } A second bug report: two orders got the same id in production.

title: Enum persistence
text: What happened and how do you recover and prevent it? After a release, 3,000 shipped orders show as NEW and 800 PAID orders show as SHIPPED . The change: a developer inserted REFUNDED in the middle of the enum. enum Status { NEW, PAID, SHIPPED } // before enum Status { NEW, PAID, REFUNDED, SHIPPED } // after @Enumerated EnumType.ORDINAL Status status; The DB column is an int. No exception was thrown.

title: Enum behaviour
text: Which classes change, and how would you design it so the next method costs one edit? Billing, reporting and refunds each contain this ladder. Product now wants NETBANKING at 1.5% and UPI free up to Rs 2,000 then 0.5%. double fee String type, double amount { if type.equals "CARD" return amount 0.02; else if type.equals "UPI" return 0; else if type.equals "WALLET" return amount 0.01; throw new IllegalArgumentException type ; }

title: Interface vs abstract class
text: When do you choose an interface over an abstract class, and what happens when two default methods collide? An interface is a contract with no state that a class can combine many of; an abstract class is for subclasses that share state and partial code, and you get only one. If two interfaces give the same default method, the class must override it and can pick one with A.super.hello .

title: Testability via interfaces
text: How do you make this testable and swappable? 200 unit tests for checkout call a real payment sandbox. Each takes about 400 ms, the suite takes 80 s, and fails roughly 1 run in 10 on network timeouts. The class: class CheckoutService { private final StripeClient stripe = new StripeClient "sk test ..." ; Receipt pay long cents { return stripe.charge cents ; } } Product also wants Razorpay support next quarter.

title: Money type migration
text: How do you migrate to integer minor units with no downtime? A pricing module stores money as double in a DECIMAL -less FLOAT column and passes double lines around. A reconciliation job shows 1,300 orders a day differing by 1 paisa from the payment provider. 40 million rows exist; checkout runs 24x7 at 300 orders per minute. 0.1 + 0.2 = 0.30000000000000004 sum 10 x 19.99 in double = 199.89999999999998

title: Enum vs data-driven types
text: When is an enum the right model and when is it a trap? What do EnumMap and EnumSet give you? An enum fits a closed set that changes only with a code release, and it can carry data and behaviour. If ops must add values at runtime, such as a new payment partner from a config table, an enum is a one-way door and I would use a row plus a strategy. EnumMap and EnumSet are array and bitset backed, faster than hash collections.

title: Evolving a published interface
text: How do you add this without breaking 14 teams, and what do you avoid? You own an internal SDK interface Notifier { void send String userId, String text ; } implemented by 14 teams' services. You need sendBatch List<String ids, String text and want a Priority argument eventually.

title: Refactor review
text: What do you say in review? A PR "refactors" pricing. Old code: double total List<double lines, String customerType { double sum = 0; for double l : lines sum += l 0 l 1 ; if customerType.equals "VIP" sum = 0.9; else if customerType.equals "EMP" sum = 0.8; return sum; } The PR adds PricingStrategyFactory , AbstractDiscountProvider and a plugin registry, and changes double to long cents in one commit with no new tests. Lines 2 x 4999 and 1 x 2000 should give VIP 10799.

title: Encapsulation
text: My class has private fields with a getter and setter for each. Is that encapsulation? Not really. Encapsulation means the object owns its data and is the only one that can change it, so its rules cannot be broken from outside. A public setter for every field lets any caller put the object into an invalid state, so it is just public fields with extra typing. I expose behaviour like withdraw cents that validates, and keep the state private.

title: Abstraction vs encapsulation
text: What is the difference between abstraction and encapsulation, and when do I use an interface versus an abstract class? Encapsulation protects data: private state behind validated methods. Abstraction simplifies what the caller sees: a stable contract like Notifier.send that hides SMTP, retries and vendor details. Interface for a contract many unrelated classes can implement; abstract class when subclasses share state or partial code and are truly the same kind of thing.

title: Overloading vs overriding
text: What is the difference between method overloading and overriding, and are fields polymorphic? Overloading means same name with different parameter lists, and javac picks one from the declared argument types at compile time. Overriding means a subclass replaces an inherited method, and the JVM picks from the actual object type at runtime. Fields and static methods are not polymorphic; they are hidden, resolved by the declared type.

title: JVM dispatch
text: Are virtual method calls slow in Java? How does the JVM actually dispatch them? Mostly no. A virtual call reads the class pointer from the object header and jumps through a fixed slot in the class's vtable. The JIT profiles each call site: with one or two seen types it inlines behind a cheap guard, so cost is near zero. Only megamorphic sites three or more types fall back to a real table call and block inlining.

title: Leaky encapsulation
text: Find the bugs, fix the class, and say what kind of decision this was. A shopping Cart is reviewed. A report job calls cart.getItems , sorts the result for display, and later the checkout total shows items in the wrong order and the cart's "last added" item is wrong. A second bug: Cart.getCreatedAt returns a java.util.Date , and a billing helper does cart.getCreatedAt .setTime ... to shift a window. class Cart { private final List<Item items = new ArrayList< ; private final Date createdAt = new Date ; public List<Item getItems { return items; } public Date getCreatedAt { return createdAt; } public void add Item i { items.add i ; } } // ReportJob List<Item sorted = cart.getItems ; Collections.sort sorted, byName ;

title: Replace if/else with dispatch
text: Which classes change for BNPL today, and how would you restructure so the next method does not repeat this? A payments module supports card, UPI, wallet and netbanking. The same switch type appears in pay , refund , fee , label and receipt : 5 places. Product now wants a fifth method, "BNPL", by next Friday. Last quarter someone added wallet and forgot refund ; 14 refunds were silently skipped. double fee String type, long cents { switch type { case "CARD": return cents 0.02; case "UPI": return 0; case "WALLET": return cents 0.005; default: throw new IllegalArgumentException type ; } }

title: Encapsulation and concurrency
text: What is wrong, how do you stop it now, and how do you fix it properly? A wallet service, 800 withdrawals/s at peak, shows 37 accounts with negative balances after a promo. Logs for one account: 12:00:01.104 t-17 withdraw acct=A91 amt=700 balance read=1000 12:00:01.104 t-23 withdraw acct=A91 amt=700 balance read=1000 12:00:01.105 t-17 balance set=300 12:00:01.105 t-23 balance set=300 <- lost update? final read says -400 in ledger The code is if acct.getBalance = amt acct.setBalance acct.getBalance - amt ; in a service class. A red herring: the DB shows no deadlocks and CPU is 30%.

title: Constructor and overriding
text: Why does it crash, and what would you change? A new AuditedReport subclass crashes with an NPE during construction in production, but only for that subclass. Stack trace: Exception in thread "main" java.lang.NullPointerException at AuditedReport.render AuditedReport.java:9 at BaseReport.<init BaseReport.java:6 at AuditedReport.<init AuditedReport.java:5 class BaseReport { BaseReport { render ; } // template call in constructor protected void render { } } class AuditedReport extends BaseReport { private final List<String lines = new ArrayList< ; AuditedReport { super ; } @Override protected void render { lines.add "start" ; } // NPE }

title: Fragile base class
text: Why 6, and what is your review comment? In review, a teammate wants to count how many elements were ever added to a set, by extending HashSet : class CountingSet<E extends HashSet<E { private int added = 0; @Override public boolean add E e { added++; return super.add e ; } @Override public boolean addAll Collection<? extends E c { added += c.size ; return super.addAll c ; } int added { return added; } } CountingSet<String s = new CountingSet< ; s.addAll List.of "a", "b", "c" ; System.out.println s.added ; // prints 6, expected 3 A second team proposes class Stack2 extends ArrayList for a stack. Both are "just reuse".

title: Megamorphic dispatch
text: Do you accept the proposal? What do you do? A pricing engine evaluates 100M Rule.apply Order calls per batch over 7 rule classes, in a random mixed list. Batch takes 410 ms of pure compute; a JMH run on a single-type list gives 35 ms. A colleague proposes replacing the Rule interface with a giant switch on an int tag "because virtual calls are slow". The whole job then writes to Postgres for 40 s. JMH: mixed 7 types 4.1 ns/op JMH: single type 0.35 ns/op Batch total wall time: 41 s compute 0.41 s, DB 40.2 s

title: Expression problem
text: Which one do you pick, and how reversible is it? A geometry library has 12 Shape types, each with area . Over the next two quarters product expects: 6 new operations perimeter, boundingBox, toSvg, toJson, collides, simplify and probably 2 new shapes. A dev says "polymorphism, put every operation as a method on each shape". Another says "make Shape a sealed interface and use pattern-matching switch in separate classes". A third module is a public SDK used by external teams.

title: All four pillars on one feature
text: Ask what you need, then sketch the model using the four pillars, and say where you would NOT use inheritance. The PM says: "Send a receipt after payment. Email for now, probably SMS and WhatsApp soon, some customers want HTML, some plain text." A dev proposes class HtmlEmailReceipt extends EmailReceipt and class PlainEmailReceipt extends EmailReceipt , and then HtmlSmsReceipt . The receipt totals are computed in ReceiptService with a getter-based Receipt bag.

title: Relationship types
text: Explain dependency, association, aggregation and composition with one example each, and how you decide which arrow to draw. Dependency: A uses B only inside a method. Association: A keeps B in a field. Aggregation: A has B but B can outlive A. Composition: A owns B, creates it and B dies with A. I decide by asking: parameter or local? field? who creates it? can it outlive the owner?

title: Aggregation vs composition
text: What is the real difference between aggregation and composition in code, not just in the diagram? In composition the whole creates the part and controls its lifetime, nobody else holds a reference, and deleting the whole deletes the parts. In aggregation the part is created elsewhere and passed in, and it survives the whole. The tell in code is new OrderLine ... inside the owner versus a part handed in through a method or constructor.

title: Coupling and cohesion
text: What are coupling and cohesion, and how would you measure or spot problems in a codebase? Coupling is how much one module must know about another; I want it low and explicit, through small interfaces. Cohesion is how well the parts of one class belong together; I want it high, one reason to change. I spot problems with fan-out, churn and size, a class touched by many teams, or one needing many mocks per test.

title: Inheritance vs realization
text: What is the difference between inheritance and realization, and why do experienced developers lean on realization? Inheritance extends , solid line with hollow triangle is is-a between classes and shares state and code. Realization implements , dashed line with hollow triangle means the class fulfils an interface contract. Realization binds you only to a contract, so it is cheap and reversible; class inheritance is the tightest coupling Java offers.

title: Hidden dependencies
text: Why flaky, and how do you fix both the tests and the design? CI has 40 tests that sporadically fail, always between 23:55 and 00:05 UTC and on month-end. All involve InvoiceService , which does Instant.now and new PdfWriter inside render . Failure sample: expected: <2026-01-31 invoice due 2026-03-02 but was: <2026-02-01 invoice due 2026-03-03 FAILED: InvoiceServiceTest.dueDateIsThirtyDaysOut 0.9 s A red herring: the team suspects the test DB.

title: Bidirectional association
text: Explain both symptoms, and decide whether the bidirectional link stays. After adding Customer.orders to an existing Order.customer link, two problems appear. The API for GET /customers/7 returns HTTP 500 with a stack trace, and the customer list page, 100 customers, becomes slow. java.lang.StackOverflowError at com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ser.BeanPropertySerializer.serializeAsField at ... Customer "orders" - Order "customer" - Customer "orders" ... SQL log: 1 query for customers + 100 queries "select from orders where customer id=?" 210 ms total

title: Lifetime and cascade
text: What went wrong in the model, and how do you clean up and prevent it? A nightly job deletes 10,000 cancelled orders. DBA reports order line has grown from 2M to 2.9M rows in 30 days although order count is flat, and storage alerts fire. The schema: CREATE TABLE order line id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY, order id BIGINT NOT NULL, -- no foreign key sku TEXT, qty INT ; -- orphan check SELECT count FROM order line ol LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.id = ol.order id WHERE o.id IS NULL; -- 900000

title: Cohesion and god class
text: What is wrong and what is your refactor plan? UserManager is 1,800 lines, changed by 5 teams, about 25 merge conflicts per quarter, and each unit test needs 3 mocks plus a 90-line setup. Fields and methods: class UserManager { private DbPool db; private SmtpClient smtp; private ImageLib img; void login String u, String p { / db / } void sendWelcome String u { / smtp / } byte resizeAvatar byte b { / img / } String generateReport String u { / db + formatting / } }

title: Aggregation delete
text: Why did songs disappear and what is the right model? A music app deleted playlist "Old stuff" 50 songs . Next morning support gets tickets: 50 songs vanished from users' libraries and from other playlists. Code and schema: @Entity class Playlist { @ManyToMany cascade = CascadeType.REMOVE // songs owned by the playlist? @JoinTable name = "playlist song" List<Song songs; } void deletePlaylist long id { playlistRepo.delete playlistRepo.getReferenceById id ; } Hibernate SQL on delete: delete from playlist song where playlist id=? delete from song where id=? -- x 50

title: Leaking owned parts
text: What relationship was intended, what did the code do instead, and how do you fix it? An Order has OrderLine s and a stored total . A bug report says orders show total Rs 4,200 while lines sum to Rs 3,700. Audit finds one caller doing order.lines .get 0 .setQty 1 . Code: class Order { private final List<OrderLine lines = new ArrayList< ; private long total; void addLine OrderLine l { lines.add l ; total += l.price l.qty ; } List<OrderLine lines { return lines; } } class OrderLine { long price; int qty; OrderLine long p, int q { price = p; qty = q; } }

title: Coupling at service level
text: Where is the coupling, what do you change first, and what do you not touch? Two services, orders and inventory , share the stock table in one Postgres. A column rename in inventory last week broke orders in production for 22 minutes error rate 9% . Both services must be released together to change anything in stock . Orders also calls inventory with a flag: reserve sku, qty, mode="STRICT" . Leadership wants "microservices, so independent teams". orders: ERROR column "qty available" does not exist x 14,200 in 22 min inventory deploy v142 at 10:03; orders unchanged since v97

title: Class diagram
text: Name the classes, draw each relationship with its type, multiplicity and reason, and say what you would NOT model. Interview prompt: "Design the class model for a library: members borrow physical copies of books; a book title can have many copies; a loan has a due date and fee rules differ for students and staff; deleting a member must not delete the book catalogue; a branch has shelves with slots." You have 10 minutes at a whiteboard.

title: DRY
text: What does DRY really mean, and is removing all duplicated-looking code always right? DRY means every piece of knowledge, like "an adult is 18 or older", lives in exactly one place. It is not about identical-looking lines. Two snippets that look the same but change for different reasons are not duplicates, and merging them creates worse coupling. I wait for the third use before extracting.

title: Demeter and tell-don't-ask
text: What is the Law of Demeter, and how is it different from "tell, don't ask"? Demeter says an object should only talk to itself, its fields, its parameters and things it created, so avoid a.getB .getC .doThing . Tell-don't-ask says put behaviour next to the data instead of pulling data out and deciding outside. Demeter limits how far you reach; tell-don't-ask decides where logic lives. They overlap but are not the same.

title: Composition over inheritance
text: Why do people say "prefer composition over inheritance", and when is inheritance still the right choice? Inheritance is the tightest coupling in the language: parent changes ripple to children, behaviour is fixed at compile time, and combining traits explodes into subclasses. Composition builds behaviour from small swappable parts, even at runtime. Inheritance is still right for a stable, true is-a with real reuse, like AbstractList .

title: Immutability
text: What makes a Java class truly immutable, and why does final on a field not guarantee it? final only stops reassigning the reference; the object it points to can still change, so a final List can be added to. A truly immutable class is final, has final fields, no setters, and makes defensive copies of mutable inputs and outputs. It is thread-safe with no locks and safe as a map key.

title: Speculative generality
text: What is your review response, and when would you accept the abstraction? A PR for "export orders to CSV" adds 600 lines: ExportStrategy , AbstractExporterFactoryProvider , and a plugin ExporterRegistry "in case we add PDF, XML, Parquet". The only requirement ticket says CSV. The author argues it will save time later. The PR has 2 bugs found in review, and the author says the sprint ends Thursday.

title: Mutable value object
text: Why does get fail, and how do you fix it at the design level? A cache keyed by a Money object returns null for prices that were clearly stored. Test log: cache.put price, "label" ; // price.cents = 500 price.add 100 ; // cents = 600 somewhere in a pricing step cache.get price - null // expected "label" size=1, containsKey=false class Money { public long cents; void add long c { cents += c; } @Override public boolean equals Object o { return o instanceof Money m && m.cents == cents; } @Override public int hashCode { return Long.hashCode cents ; } }

title: Tell, don't ask
text: What are the two distinct problems, and what is the fix? A support ticket: 3 accounts overdrawn on the same minute. The code in 12 callers repeats the pattern; one caller forgot the status check. if account.getBalance = amount && account.getStatus == Status.ACTIVE { account.setBalance account.getBalance - amount ; } else { throw new IllegalStateException ; } t-4 read bal=1000 ; t-9 read bal=1000 ; t-4 set 300 ; t-9 set 300 - two 700 withdrawals, balance 300 audit: 7 of 12 callers check status, 5 do not

title: Fail fast
text: What principle was broken, and what do you change in code and platform? A payments service deploys with PAYMENT API KEY missing from config typo in the env var name . Health check is green. 40 minutes later the first payment fails and 312 customers see errors. 10:02 deploy ok, readiness: UP 10:41 ERROR PaymentClient - apiKey is null 10:41 NullPointerException at PaymentClient.charge PaymentClient.java:57 error rate 100% on /pay since 10:41, orders 312 failed The endpoint also accepts amount as an unchecked String from Map<String,Object . Red herring: the payment vendor status page is green.

title: Demeter refactor
text: How do you make this change cheap, and how do you avoid turning Order into a middle man? Product wants to replace Address.city a String with a Location object city, region, geohash . A grep shows: order.getCustomer .getAddress .getCity - 40 call sites in 18 files order.getCustomer .getAddress .getCountry .getTaxRule .rate - 9 sites Estimated change: 2.5 days and 6 reviewers. Meanwhile Order already has 28 delegating methods that nobody wants more of.

title: DRY vs decoupling
text: Do you extract the shared library? Defend it and give the reversibility. Two services checkout , notifications each format phone numbers with 6 identical lines. A reviewer says: "Extract a shared library, DRY." Facts: checkout is released daily, notifications weekly; formatting rules will diverge per country soon notifications needs E.164 for the SMS vendor, checkout needs display format ; a shared library last year forced a 2-service lockstep release that took 3 hours.

title: KISS
text: What do you ask first, and what do you recommend? A team of 4 proposes for a new internal "leave request" feature: a message broker, three microservices requests, approvals, notifications and a saga. Expected load: 200 requests per day, about 5 per minute at peak. They estimate 3 months. Another engineer says "one app and one DB transaction, 2 weeks". The CTO asks you for a recommendation on a whiteboard. peak: 5 req/min ; single db.t3.medium-class instance handles 100x that verify with a load test ops cost of proposal: 3 pipelines, broker cluster, tracing, 3 on-call surfaces

title: Fail fast vs availability
text: Where should the job fail fast and where should it not? Propose the design. A nightly import processes 2 million CSV rows into the catalogue. The current code throws on the first malformed row; one bad row at line 1,704,221 aborts the job after 3 hours and the next day's prices are stale. A new engineer says "fail fast is a principle, keep it". Another wants to wrap everything in catch Exception e { log } . 03:12 ERROR ImportJob - NumberFormatException: "12,5O" at row 1704221 03:12 job FAILED after 3h 02m ; 1,704,220 rows rolled back

title: Why SOLID
text: What is SOLID and why should a developer care about it? SOLID is five design habits Single responsibility, Open/closed, Liskov, Interface segregation, Dependency inversion whose one goal is that a change lands in one place. Code is edited for years, so the real cost is how many files I touch and re-test per feature. It is a guide, not a law: on a 200-line app it is over-engineering.

title: SRP definition
text: What does the Single Responsibility Principle actually say? Does it mean a class should have only one method? SRP says a class should have one reason to change, meaning it answers to one stakeholder or concern. It does not mean one method. If finance and marketing can each force me to edit the same class, it has two responsibilities.

title: OCP definition
text: Explain the Open/Closed Principle with a concrete example. Does "closed" mean you can never edit a file? Open for extension, closed for modification: adding behaviour should mean adding new code, not editing tested code. I depend on an interface and add an implementation. Closed does not forbid bug fixes; it targets the if/else on type that grows with every feature.

title: Interface vs enum vs sealed
text: You need to vary behaviour by payment type. When do you choose an interface, an enum with behaviour, or a sealed type? Open set that third parties may extend: interface/Strategy. Closed set I own, where I want the compiler to know every case: enum with behaviour. Closed hierarchy with different data per case: sealed type plus exhaustive when , so adding a case becomes a compile error everywhere it matters.

title: Refactor God class
text: Which smells do you see, what classes would you extract, and in what order do you refactor? A ReportGenerator 900 lines, 4 owners in git blame has queryDb , generatePdf , generateCsv and email . Product wants Excel next sprint. Last quarter 3 of 5 releases touching this file caused a regression in unrelated output. There are no unit tests, only a manual QA checklist. class ReportGenerator { byte generate String format, int id { List<Row rows = jdbc.query "select ...", id ; if format.equals "pdf" { / 300 lines / } else if format.equals "csv" { / 80 lines / } mailer.send user.email, bytes ; return bytes; } }

title: Requirement change
text: Which classes change for the Black Friday rule today, and how would you restructure so the next campaign needs no edits to old code? An order system computes price with a Pricing.total order method containing a switch customer.tier for REGULAR, STUDENT, VIP. Marketing now adds a Black Friday 40% rule and a coupon rule, each requested separately, and says more campaign rules arrive monthly. Team of 6, 3 deploys a week. The switch is already 90 lines and has 14 tests.

title: Over-splitting
text: How do you review this? A junior's PR for a 120-line UserRegistration flow adds 14 classes: UserNameValidator , UserEmailValidator , UserPasswordHasher , UserIdGenerator , UserSaver , UserRegistrationFacade , UserRegistrationFacadeImpl and more. Each has one method and one implementation. The PR description says "applied SRP everywhere". Build time and navigation cost went up; a one-field change now touches 5 files.

title: instanceof chain
text: What is wrong structurally, what is the immediate bug, and how do you fix it so it cannot recur? A notification module has this code and a bug report: "WhatsApp messages never get a retry, SMS does". The team added WhatsApp last week. void send Notifier n, String msg { if n instanceof SmsNotifier { n.send msg ; retry n, msg, 3 ; } else if n instanceof EmailNotifier { n.send msg ; } else { n.send msg ; } // WhatsApp falls here }

title: Testability of SRP
text: What do you change in the design to cut test time and flakiness, and what would you still leave as integration tests? PaymentService.pay validates the card, calls a gateway over HTTP, writes to MySQL and sends an email. Its unit test takes 3.2 s Testcontainers MySQL plus a WireMock server , the suite of 400 such tests takes 21 minutes in CI, and developers skip it locally. Flaky rate is 4% per run, mostly the SMTP stub.

title: Wrong seam
text: What went wrong with the OCP application, and what do you do now? Six months ago the team introduced ShippingStrategy STANDARD, EXPRESS "for OCP". Now product asks for: free shipping above 999 for all methods, a holiday surcharge on all methods, and carrier-specific cut-off times. Each requirement forces changes to ShippingStrategy.cost signature and all implementations; PRs touch 9 files, and the original interface has 2 implementations only.

title: Sealed vs interface
text: How do you migrate so WALLET ships safely now and partner methods become possible later? Backend models Payment as an enum PaymentType {CARD, UPI, NETBANKING} with 11 switch statements across 7 services. Product wants to add WALLET and, next quarter, partner-provided methods from external jars. A previous addition of NETBANKING missed one switch and shipped a null fee for 2 hours about 3,000 orders . Deploys are daily; no downtime allowed.

title: Ambiguous requirement
text: How do you approach the design, and how do you decide how much SOLID to apply? In an interview you are told: "Design the discount system for our app so it is flexible." Nothing else. You have 35 minutes. A teammate shows a 40-class design from a past project rules engine, DSL, plugin loader and says SOLID demands it.

title: LSP contract
text: What is the Liskov Substitution Principle? Give an example other than Square and Rectangle. If code works with a base type, it must keep working with any subtype. A subclass may accept more and promise more, but must not accept less, promise less, break invariants or throw surprising exceptions. Example: Penguin extends Bird with fly throwing; a loop over 1,000 birds crashes on the first penguin.

title: ISP
text: What does the Interface Segregation Principle say, and how is it different from SRP? Clients should not be forced to depend on methods they do not use, so I prefer several small interfaces over one fat one. SRP is about a class's reasons to change; ISP is about what a client sees. A fat interface causes empty or throwing implementations, needless recompiles and heavy mocks.

title: DIP vs DI
text: What is the Dependency Inversion Principle, and is it the same as Dependency Injection? DIP: high-level policy should not depend on low-level detail; both depend on an abstraction, and the abstraction is owned by the high-level side. Dependency Injection is one technique to supply the implementation. DIP is the design rule, DI is the wiring.

title: Fake vs mock vs stub
text: How does dependency injection improve testing, and what is the difference between a stub, a fake and a mock? With constructor injection a class receives collaborators, so a test passes a lightweight version instead of a DB. A stub returns canned data, a fake is a working light implementation like an in-memory map, a mock verifies calls. I prefer fakes for state and mocks sparingly for interactions like "email sent once".

title: LSP violation
text: What is the principle at stake, who is at fault, and how do you fix it? A nightly job crashes with this stack at 02:14, after processing 4,100 of 9,000 records: java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException at java.util.Collections$UnmodifiableCollection.add Collections.java:1060 at com.shop.Exporter.addHeaders Exporter.java:37 class Exporter { void export List<String columns { columns.add 0, "id" ; // add header // ... } } // caller 1: exporter.export new ArrayList< cols // caller 2: exporter.export config.columns // returns List.copyOf ...

title: Fat interface
text: How do you split it without a big-bang change? UserRepository has 14 methods findById , findByEmail , save , delete , purge , exportAll , ... . The profile screen only reads names, the admin tool deletes, the nightly job exports. Each screen test mocks all 14 methods about 25 lines of setup . Last month a profile-screen bug deleted a user because someone injected the full repo and called delete by mistake.

title: Interface on wrong side
text: Does this follow DIP? What do you ask them to change? Module layout in a review: :domain OrderService, Order :data MySqlOrderRepository, OrderRepository interface, JPA entities :domain depends on :data The author says "we use DIP: OrderService talks to the OrderRepository interface". Yet last week a JPA upgrade forced edits in :domain , and domain unit tests need the JPA jar on the classpath build 90 s .

title: Untestable `new`
text: How do you make it testable and what would you assert? class InvoiceMailer { void sendMonthly long userId { User u = new UserDao .find userId ; String body = new TemplateEngine .render "invoice", u ; new SmtpClient "smtp.corp" .send u.email , body ; } } The team wants a test that checks the email contains the user's name. Currently it requires a live DB and SMTP; a colleague suggests PowerMock to intercept new .

title: Constructor bloat
text: What do you do? CheckoutService has a constructor with 9 injected dependencies CartRepo , PriceCalc , TaxClient , PaymentGateway , InventoryClient , Mailer , AuditLog , Metrics , Clock . Tests need 9 mocks and 40 lines of setup. A teammate proposes switching to field injection with @Autowired "to cut the noise", another proposes a service locator Locator.get Tax.class .

title: Service locator migration
text: How do you migrate to constructor injection safely? A 300-class Android/backend app calls a global ServiceLocator.get PaymentGateway::class inside methods in about 120 places. Tests mutate the global in @Before and sometimes forget to reset, causing order-dependent failures about 3% flaky, one failure rerun per day . Releases are weekly; there is no freeze. Management wants no big-bang.

title: Strengthened precondition
text: Which LSP rules does WalletPayment break and how do you redesign? abstract class PaymentMethod { / Charges amount in rupees, amount 0 / abstract Receipt charge Money amt ; } class CardPayment extends PaymentMethod { Receipt charge Money amt { / ok / } } class WalletPayment extends PaymentMethod { Receipt charge Money amt { if amt.rupees 10 000 throw new LimitExceededException ; if balance < amt.rupees return null; // null on insufficient balance / ... / } } Checkout calls method.charge total .id for every method. In production, wallet orders above 10k throw an unexpected exception and low-balance orders produce an NPE; 1.2% of checkouts fail with 500s.

title: Combining the five
text: Present the design. Design the notification part of an order system in 10 minutes: when an order is placed, notify by email and push; SMS comes next quarter; push provider times out about 2% of the time and must not block order placement; tests must not send real messages. The interviewer asks you to justify the design in SOLID terms and say where you would NOT apply it.

title: Which diagram
text: In an LLD interview, which UML diagrams do you actually draw, and how do you pick one? Five sketches: class diagram for structure, sequence for calls over time, state for one object's lifecycle, use-case for who does what, activity for a workflow. I pick by the question: structure means class, order of calls means sequence, lifecycle means state. I draw the smallest one that answers it.

title: Composition vs aggregation
text: In a class diagram, what is the difference between association, aggregation and composition, and how do they show up in code? Association: A knows or uses B field or parameter . Aggregation: A has B but B can live alone, like Team and Players. Composition: A owns B and B dies with A, like House and Rooms. I choose by asking "does the part die with the whole?".

title: State diagram to code
text: How do you turn a state diagram into code, and when do you choose an enum versus the State pattern? A state diagram lists states and the events that move between them. Simple case: an enum with a canGoTo table. If each state has rich behaviour, I use the State pattern: one class per state. Illegal transitions are the missing cells, and they also become my test cases. Concurrent events need a lock or compare-and-set.

title: include vs extend
text: What does a use-case diagram show, and what is the difference between <<include and <<extend ? It shows who actors uses the system for what use cases and nothing about how. <<include means the base use case always runs another one, like Withdraw includes Authenticate PIN. <<extend is an optional addition, like Print receipt extending Deposit. Include arrow points to the included; extend arrow points to the base.

title: Class model for stated problem
text: Sketch the classes and relationships, and show how the new requirement fits. Interview prompt: "Library: members borrow books, max 5 books at a time, a fine applies after 14 days, a book can have several copies." You have 2 minutes at the whiteboard. The interviewer will next add "reserve a book that is out" and watch how your diagram absorbs it.

title: Sequence with failure
text: Redraw it so it makes the point, and map it to code. Interviewer: "Show me what happens when a user places an order. Payment can fail." You have 1 minute. The participants are Client, Controller, OrderService, PaymentGateway, Repo. Your first attempt shows every internal call including logging and validation, and the diagram has 20 arrows.

title: State race
text: What is wrong, and how do you fix it? Orders table shows 37 orders last week with state='CANCELLED' but a shipment was created. Logs for one of them: 10:01:02.113 payment-callback order=881 load state=CREATED 10:01:02.115 cancel-api order=881 load state=CREATED 10:01:02.140 payment-callback order=881 set state=PAID canGoTo ok 10:01:02.152 cancel-api order=881 set state=CANCELLED canGoTo ok 10:01:03.001 shipper order=881 saw PAID earlier - shipment created The code uses the enum canGoTo table from the state diagram; unit tests for every illegal transition pass.

title: Parallel branches
text: What does the diagram miss, and how do you change the design? A checkout activity diagram shows "Charge card" 800 ms and "Reserve stock" 300 ms in parallel after "Validate cart", then "Send confirmation". The team implemented it with coroutineScope { async {charge}; async {reserve} } . In production, about 0.4% of orders end with the card charged but stock not reserved out of stock race , and finance counts 120 such orders last month.

title: Diagram does not match code
text: Review the diagram against the code. What do you flag? A design doc diagram says Order < ---- OrderLine composition and Team < ---- Player aggregation . The code in the PR: class Order { private final List<OrderLine lines; Order List<OrderLine lines { this.lines = lines; } // caller owns the list } class Team { private final List<Player players = new ArrayList< ; Team String name { players.add new Player "captain" ; } } Another arrow in the doc shows Circle ---- Shape with the arrowhead at Circle.

title: Missing actor
text: How should you have scoped the use cases, and how do you patch the design now? Prompt: "Design a ride-booking backend." The interviewer says only that riders request rides and drivers accept. Your first use-case diagram has Rider and Driver. Later in the interview the interviewer asks "who triggers payment after the trip, who expires an unaccepted request after 2 minutes, and who handles support refunds?" and your design has no owner for these.

title: Async vs sync in sequence
text: Redraw the sequence to meet the SLO and say how it changes the code. A diagram for "upload photo" shows Client, API, Storage, Thumbnailer, Notifier with all solid arrows. In production, uploads of 8 MB take 6 s end to end because the API waits for thumbnail generation 4 s and the push notification 500 ms before replying. The SLO is a 1 s response. Thumbnailer fails about 1% of the time and the client sees errors even though the photo was stored.

title: Time-boxed drawing
text: Recover the round: what do you cut, what do you say, and where does the weekend rule go? 45-minute LLD round for a parking lot. At minute 12 you are still polishing a class diagram with 14 classes, getters and setters, and visibility marks on every field. The interviewer glances at the clock: no code yet. At minute 14 they add: "And pricing should differ for weekends." You notice the diagram does not show where that fits.

title: Singleton basics
text: What is the Singleton pattern, when would you use it, and what are the minimum ingredients to implement it? Singleton guarantees one instance of a class and gives a global access point. Ingredients: a private constructor so nobody else can new it, and a static method returning the single instance. Good for immutable config, a metrics registry or a connection-pool manager. It is global state with controlled creation, which is also why it is risky.

title: Double-checked locking
text: Why does double-checked locking need volatile ? Walk through what can go wrong without it. new Config is three steps: allocate, run the constructor, assign the reference. Without volatile , the JIT or CPU can reorder so the reference is published before the constructor finishes, and another thread sees a non-null but half-built object. Since Java 5 JSR-133 , volatile forbids that reordering and guarantees visibility.

title: Factory Method idea
text: What is the Factory Method pattern, and how is it different from a static factory method like List.of ? Factory Method defines an interface for creating an object but lets subclasses or implementations decide which class to instantiate, so the caller depends on a product interface, not a concrete class. It solves if type == "sms" new Sms ... repeated in many places. A static factory method like List.of is just a named constructor; the GoF Factory Method has the subclass decide.

title: Singleton anti-pattern
text: Why do many engineers call Singleton an anti-pattern, and what do you use instead? A Singleton is hidden global state: hidden dependencies the constructor does not say it needs Config , hard to test state leaks between tests, you cannot swap a fake , tight coupling to a concrete class, concurrency issues with mutable state, and it mixes the class's job with controlling its own lifetime. Instead I inject the dependency and let a container or the composition root create one instance.

title: Naive lazy
text: Explain the bug, evaluate both proposals and choose the fix. A service opens a rate-limiter in getInstance . Under load tests with 64 threads, the limiter allows about 2x the configured 100 req/s, and a debug log shows "RateLimiter created" twice at startup. public static RateLimiter getInstance { if instance == null { instance = new RateLimiter 100 ; } return instance; } A teammate says the window is tiny and proposes synchronized on the whole method. Another says "just make it volatile".

title: DCL without volatile
text: Diagnose the incident and fix it. A pricing service migrates from 4-core to 64-core hosts. After the move, about 1 in 20,000 requests throws NullPointerException in PriceTable.lookup , and never on the old hosts or in staging. Stack excerpt and code: java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot read field "rates" because "this.table" is null at com.shop.PriceTable.lookup PriceTable.java:41 at com.shop.Pricing.price Pricing.java:88 public final class PriceTable { private static PriceTable instance; // no volatile private final Map<String, Double rates; private PriceTable { rates = loadRates ; } // 15 ms public static PriceTable getInstance { if instance == null { synchronized PriceTable.class { if instance == null instance = new PriceTable ; } } return instance; } }

title: Singleton to DI
text: Refactor it for testability without losing the "one instance" property in production. A payments module uses Config.getInstance and Logger.getInstance inside PaymentService.pay . The test suite has 60 tests; run alone, each passes, run together, 3 fail depending on order a test sets Config.set "retries","0" and never resets it . A new test needs a fake stripe key and cannot supply one. class PaymentService { void pay Order o { String key = Config.getInstance .get "stripe.key" ; Logger.getInstance .log "paying " + o.id ; // ... } }

title: New channel requirement
text: Which classes change for push today, and how do you restructure so WhatsApp is a one-class change? AlertService.alert type, msg has an if/else on "sms" and "email" , and the same if appears in 5 other classes AuditNotifier , RetryJob , ... . Product asks for push notifications this sprint and WhatsApp next quarter. Last time a channel was added, one of the 6 places was missed and critical alerts silently went nowhere for 3 days. if type.equals "sms" new SmsNotifier .send msg ; else if type.equals "email" new EmailNotifier .send msg ;

title: Over-engineering
text: How do you review it, and when would you accept a factory? A PR in a 500-line module adds UserFactory , IUserFactory , UserFactoryImpl and UserCreator , all just to call new User name, email . The author says "for flexibility, and it is a pattern". There is one User class, no variation, no tests that need a fake. Another PR for ArrayList creation adds ListFactory .

title: Choosing creational approach
text: Which creational approach do you pick and what do you leave out? A codebase has 40 call sites doing new SmsSender "key" . Product wants WhatsApp, and ops wants to switch SMS vendors per country India vs EU , with a kill switch. A teammate proposes Abstract Factory plus Builder plus Prototype "to be ready for anything". You have two days.

title: Breaking a Singleton
text: Explain each way the guarantee breaks and how you fix them. A licence-manager Singleton private constructor, holder idiom allows 10 seats. QA reports 12 concurrent users got in. Findings: 1 a plugin deserializes a saved session object that contains the manager, 2 the app runs on an app server where two web apps each ship the jar in their own class loader, 3 a test helper calls the constructor via reflection. public final class LicenseManager implements Serializable { private LicenseManager {} private static class Holder { static final LicenseManager I = new LicenseManager ; } public static LicenseManager getInstance { return Holder.I; } private final AtomicInteger seats = new AtomicInteger 10 ; }

title: Eager init failure
text: Explain why one missing file poisons the endpoint permanently, and how you fix it. After a deploy, a service starts but every request to /prices returns 500. Logs: java.lang.ExceptionInInitializerError at com.shop.PriceApi.handle PriceApi.java:22 Caused by: java.io.FileNotFoundException: /etc/shop/rates.json at com.shop.RateConfig.<clinit RateConfig.java:9 ... java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: Could not initialize class com.shop.RateConfig at com.shop.PriceApi.handle PriceApi.java:22 all later requests public final class RateConfig { private static final RateConfig INSTANCE = new RateConfig ; // reads /etc/shop/rates.json private RateConfig { / load file / } public static RateConfig getInstance { return INSTANCE; } } The file was present on the previous hosts; it appeared 40 s after the container started on the new platform. Other endpoints work fine.

title: Abstract Factory vs Factory Method
text: What is Abstract Factory, and how is it different from Factory Method? Factory Method creates one product and lets a subclass or registry choose which class. Abstract Factory is one interface that creates a whole family of related products so they always match, for example a Stripe client, Stripe webhook verifier and Stripe refund service together. I reach for it when mixing parts from two families would be a bug.

title: Why Builder exists
text: What problem does the Builder pattern solve? Why not just use a constructor or setters? Builder assembles a complex object step by step with named optional parameters, validates in build , and returns an immutable object. Constructors with many arguments are unreadable and swap-prone, and setters leave the object half-built and mutable between calls.

title: Builder validation
text: What is wrong with this builder and how would you fix it? Code review of a notification service. Production shows NullPointerException in the sender thread, and one push went out with retries = -1 that retried forever and hit the provider rate limit about 4,000 retries in a minute for one user . public final class Notification { private final String title, body; private final int retries; private Notification Builder b { title = b.title; body = b.body; retries = b.retries; } public static class Builder { String title, body; int retries; public Builder title String t { title = t; return this; } public Builder body String b { body = b; return this; } public Builder retries int r { retries = r; return this; } public Notification build { return new Notification this ; } } }

title: Adding a new product kind
text: Which classes change for each of the two requirements, and what does that tell you about the pattern's trade-off? Your PaymentsFactory has two implementations StripeFactory , RazorpayFactory and three products: client, verifier, refunds. Product asks for DisputeService next sprint, and a third provider PayPal in Q4. Both providers must support disputes; PayPal supports everything.

title: Builder in Kotlin
text: Do you still need the Builder pattern in Kotlin? When would you write one anyway? Mostly no. Kotlin has named and default arguments, copy on data classes, and init { require ... } for validation, which cover optional parameters and invariants. I still write a builder or a lambda-with-receiver DSL for step-by-step or order-dependent assembly, when Java callers need to use the class, or when the object is built over time a request assembled across layers .

title: Telescoping constructor
text: Refactor it. Which pattern, what does the new code look like, and how do you migrate 140 call sites safely? You inherit this class used in 140 places. Two incidents in a quarter came from swapped arguments connectTimeoutMs and readTimeoutMs both int . public class HttpClientConfig { public HttpClientConfig String baseUrl {...} public HttpClientConfig String baseUrl, int connectTimeoutMs {...} public HttpClientConfig String baseUrl, int connectTimeoutMs, int readTimeoutMs {...} public HttpClientConfig String baseUrl, int connectTimeoutMs, int readTimeoutMs, boolean followRedirects, int maxRetries {...} }

title: Over-engineering
text: What is your review comment? A PR adds this for a service that talks to exactly one email provider SES and has no plan for another. interface EmailFactory { Sender sender ; Template template ; } class SesEmailFactory implements EmailFactory { public Sender sender { return new SesSender ; } public Template template { return new SesTemplate ; } } class EmailFactoryProvider { static EmailFactory get { return new SesEmailFactory ; } } The author says "future-proofing". Sender and Template do not need to match each other in any way.

title: Director
text: How would you restructure this, and which pattern fits? A reporting module produces the same monthly report title, 20 rows, footer as HTML for email and PDF for download. Today two classes, HtmlReportGenerator and PdfReportGenerator , each repeat the same ordering logic title, rows, totals, footer . Last month someone added a totals row to HTML only and the PDF drifted for two weeks.

title: Step builder trade-off
text: What is a step staged builder, and when is it worth the extra interfaces compared with a fluent builder that validates in build ? A step builder returns a different interface after each required step, so the compiler enforces the required fields and their order: builder .url x returns NeedsMethod , then .method .. returns the optional stage with build . A normal builder catches missing fields at runtime in build . I use the step builder for public APIs where a missing required field is a costly bug and the required list is short and stable, not for a 4-field internal class.

title: Mixed families
text: Diagnose and fix it. A checkout service supports Stripe and Razorpay. After a "dynamic config" change that reloads the provider flag without restart, about 0.3% of webhooks roughly 90 per hour out of 30,000 fail signature verification with invalid signature . Charges succeed. The code: class CheckoutService { private final Config cfg; Client client { return cfg.provider .equals "stripe" ? new StripeClient k : new RazorpayClient k ; } WebhookVerifier verifier { return cfg.provider .equals "stripe" ? new StripeVerifier s : new RazorpayVerifier s ; } } Failures cluster within 2 minutes after each flag change. CPU, DB and network look normal.

title: DI as abstract factory
text: Do you agree? What do you build instead, and when would a hand-written Abstract Factory still win? You are designing a notification module. Environments: dev console log notifier , staging sandbox SMS/email , prod real SMS/email . The team uses Spring Boot. A colleague proposes hand-written NotifierFactory classes per environment, selected by a static FactoryProvider.get . Tests currently need to set a system property to switch the factory.

title: Builder reuse bug
text: Find the bugs and fix them. Is it also a thread-safety problem? A batch job builds 10,000 emails reusing one builder to "save allocations". Customers report seeing other customers' CC addresses. Code: EmailBuilder b = new EmailBuilder ; // fields: to, List<String cc = new ArrayList< for Customer c : customers { b.to c.email ; if c.hasManager b.addCc c.managerEmail ; send b.build ; } // build : return new Email to, cc ; // passes the same list reference Logs show email number 4,112 had 38 CC addresses.

title: Prototype idea
text: What is the Prototype pattern and when does copying an object beat constructing a new one? Prototype creates new objects by copying a configured existing one. It pays off when construction is expensive parsing, I/O, a large graph or when I want many variations of a template. I share the immutable heavy parts and copy only the mutable state. If new is cheap, copying is just extra complexity.

title: Object Pool idea
text: What is an Object Pool, and what are the rules for using one correctly? An Object Pool keeps ready-made reusable objects and lends them out instead of creating and destroying them per use. It is worth it for expensive or scarce resources: DB connections, threads, big buffers. Rules: bound the size, always release in finally , reset state on release, and validate or expire stale objects.

title: Shallow copy
text: Explain the bug and fix it. How would you test it? A "duplicate report" feature lets users clone a report template and edit rows. Support tickets: "editing my copy changes the original". The code: class Report implements Cloneable { String name; List<String rows = new ArrayList< ; @Override public Report clone { try { return Report super.clone ; } catch CloneNotSupportedException e { throw new AssertionError e ; } } } Report copy = original.clone ; copy.rows.add "Q4 total" ; After the call, original.rows.size is 1 larger.

title: Pool exhaustion
text: Walk me through diagnosis and fix. An order API runs 6 pods, HikariCP maximumPoolSize=10 each. At 21:05 latency goes from 80 ms to 30 s and errors show: HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms. HikariPool stats: total=10 active=10 idle=0 waiting=87 DB CPU is 12%, Postgres pg stat activity shows 10 per pod, many in idle in transaction . A deploy shipped at 21:00 with a new refundOrder method. Traffic is normal at 450 req/s.

title: DI vs Service Locator
text: What is dependency injection, how is it different from a DI container and from a Service Locator, and which injection style do you prefer? DI means an object receives its collaborators from outside instead of creating or looking them up. A container such as Spring or Dagger is a tool that automates the wiring; DI works without it. A Service Locator, where a class calls Container.get X.class inside methods, hides dependencies and is not DI. I prefer constructor injection: the object is valid when built and fields can be final .

title: Testability
text: How do you make it testable, and what do the tests look like? OrderService is untestable: every test hits Stripe's sandbox, takes 1.4 s, and fails when the network is down. A live key is in source control. class OrderService { private final PaymentGateway gw = new StripeGateway "sk live ..." ; private final Clock clock = Clock.systemUTC ; void place Order o { if o.createdAt .isBefore Instant.now clock .minusSeconds 900 throw new ExpiredException ; gw.charge o ; } } You have 1 day. 300 unit tests will use this class.

title: Pooling cheap objects
text: What is your review decision and reasoning? A PR introduces a StringBuilderPool and a RequestDtoPool DTOs of 5 small fields "to reduce GC". The service handles 3,000 req/s, GC logs show young collections every 2 s taking 4 ms, and p99 latency is 60 ms dominated by DB calls. The author has no benchmark. RequestDto dto = dtoPool.borrow ; try { fill dto ; handle dto ; } finally { dto.clear ; dtoPool.release dto ; }

title: Prototype and identity
text: What is wrong with copy ? How would you correct it? A "duplicate product" feature copies a Product prototype. Afterwards the catalog shows two rows with the same SKU, and inventory updates apply to both. A DBA reports a unique index violation only on one path. class Product { final String id; String sku; List<Image images; Lock lock = new ReentrantLock ; Product copy { return new Product id, sku, images, lock ; } }

title: clone() vs copy constructor
text: Why do many Java engineers avoid Object.clone , and what do you use instead? How does the answer change for immutable objects and Kotlin data classes? Object.clone skips constructors, copies shallowly, cannot reassign final fields, and relies on a Cloneable marker with no method, so the contract is vague and bug-prone. I use a copy constructor or copy factory for mutable objects, and for immutable objects I do not copy at all: sharing is safe. In Kotlin copy on a data class is shallow, fine when the nested parts are immutable.

title: Pool sizing
text: What pool configuration do you propose? Show the math. Black Friday is 10x normal: 450 req/s becomes 4,500 req/s. Each request holds a connection for about 15 ms. You run 12 pods, maximumPoolSize=10 . A teammate proposes maximumPoolSize=200 per pod because "10x traffic". Postgres is max connections=500 on 8 vCPUs; pg stat activity currently shows 120 connections.

title: Dirty and stale pooled objects
text: Diagnose both symptoms and fix them. A homegrown Pool<Connection is used by a batch service. Two symptoms: 1 intermittent Connection reset errors after quiet nights, first request of the morning fails; 2 some queries run with READ ONLY mode set by a previous borrower, so writes fail with cannot execute INSERT in a read-only transaction . Logs excerpt: 05:58:01 WARN borrow - conn 7 used 11h ago 05:58:01 ERROR org.postgresql.util.PSQLException: An I/O error occurred while sending to the backend. Connection reset 09:14:22 ERROR cannot execute INSERT in a read-only transaction conn 3 The DB's idle timeout is 8 hours; a firewall drops idle TCP after 1 hour.

title: Over-injection and runtime selection
text: What do you do about the constructor, the per-request notifier choice and the two suggestions? CheckoutService has this constructor, and a new requirement arrives: pick SMS or email per request based on user preference. CheckoutService PaymentGateway g, TaxCalc t, Inventory i, SmsNotifier s, EmailNotifier e, Analytics a, AuditLog l, Clock c, Coupons cp {...} A dev suggests injecting the whole Spring ApplicationContext and calling ctx.getBean ... per request. Another suggests field injection to "shorten" the constructor.

title: What LLD tests
text: What is an LLD interview actually testing, and how is it different from a pattern quiz? It tests whether I can turn a vague idea into clean, extensible, working classes in about 45 to 60 minutes. The interviewer scores clarifying questions, sensible entities and responsibilities, extensibility, correct readable code, edge cases and concurrency, and how I communicate trade-offs. Patterns are tools I use when something varies, not the goal.

title: Clarifying requirements
text: What do you ask in the first minutes of an LLD problem, and how do you avoid asking too much? I spend 5 to 8 minutes on a few buckets: actors, the 3 to 5 core use cases, scale and shape, rules pricing, limits, failures , and out of scope. I ask the roughly six questions that change the design, write the functional and non-functional list on the board, and confirm it back with the interviewer.

title: Ambiguous requirement
text: What do you ask and what do you write down? How do you decide when to stop asking? The interviewer says only: "Design a food delivery order system." You have 45 minutes. The interviewer is deliberately vague and will answer questions but not volunteer anything. Last candidate spent 15 minutes asking 25 questions and had 10 minutes left to code.

title: Time management
text: What do you do in the next minute and how do you use the remaining 23 minutes? It is minute 22 of a 45-minute round for an elevator system. You have a polished class diagram with 14 classes Elevator, Floor, Request, Scheduler, Door, Display, Panel, ... but no code, and you have not decided whether to code. The interviewer glances at the clock.

title: Naming and class design
text: What do you flag and how do you rewrite it? A candidate's parking code in a live round: class Manager { public List<Object data; public int t; void doIt int x, int y, boolean b { ... } static Map<String, Object cache = new HashMap< ; } The interviewer asks you, as a mock reviewer, to give feedback and show the rewrite for "park a vehicle and compute the fee".

title: Extensibility answer
text: The interviewer asks "what if we add X?". How do you structure the answer, and where do you place seams without over-engineering? I answer with: which class changes, which do not, and why. For example: "Vehicle type is an enum with a mapping in one place; a new type adds one enum value and a mapping, Ticket and Level do not change." I prepare seams only for the two or three likely changes found during clarification pricing strategy, vehicle type, notification , and for the rest I say how I would refactor.

title: Requirement changes
text: Which classes change and which stay untouched? Show the edits. Your parking lot design has SpotType {COMPACT, REGULAR, LARGE} , Spot , Level , Ticket , PricingStrategy , SpotAllocator . At minute 40 the interviewer says: "Add EV charging spots with charging time billed separately, and a weekend surge price."

title: Scoring rubric
text: Who do you recommend and why? Map to a rubric. You are asked to compare two candidates on "design a rate limiter". Candidate A: Strategy, Factory, Observer and Singleton, five interfaces, code does not run, no edge cases, no concurrency mention. Candidate B: three classes, runs, handles first request, burst and clock edge, uses AtomicLong /lock correctly, explains how to add a sliding-window algorithm, one test. Both talked clearly.

title: Taking hints
text: What went wrong and how should the answer go? Mid-round on a parking lot, the interviewer asks: "What happens if two cars arrive at the same time and there is one spot left?" You answer, "That would be a database problem; we don't have that here," and keep coding. The interviewer repeats the question with different words 5 minutes later.

title: Communication and recovery
text: How do you communicate decisions during an LLD round, and what do you do when you get stuck or find your own mistake? Each decision gets one sentence: choice, reason, alternative " Map<String,Ticket for O 1 lookup; the alternative is a list scan, O n " . If stuck, I name what I am stuck on, pick one option with its trade-off, continue, and offer to revisit. If I find a mistake, I say so and fix it quickly. I finish with a dry run using concrete values.

title: Late-discovered mistake
text: What do you say and do? At minute 38 of a library-management round, while doing the dry run, you notice Library.checkout allows borrowing an already-borrowed copy: you modelled Book and Copy as one class, so there is no per-copy state. There are 7 minutes left and 200 lines written.

title: Seams vs over-engineering
text: Which do you keep and which do you cut? How do you defend the choice? In a ride-sharing LLD round you proposed RideMatchingStrategy , PricingStrategy , NotificationObserver , PaymentFactory , DriverRepository and AuditLogger . The interviewer says: "That is six abstractions for a 45-minute problem, and some have one implementation. Justify them." You have 15 minutes left.

title: Race conditions in LLD
text: Why does concurrency come up in nearly every LLD problem, and how do you approach shared state in an interview? Most LLD systems parking lot, booking, rate limiter, inventory have shared mutable state touched by many threads. A race condition means the result depends on timing, such as two threads reading count = 5 and both writing 6, losing an update. My approach: list the shared mutable data, choose a guard for each lock, atomic, concurrent collection, or avoid sharing , keep critical sections tiny, and say what I did not make thread-safe.

title: synchronized vs ReentrantLock
text: When would you use synchronized and when ReentrantLock ? What rules keep locking safe? synchronized is the simplest and auto-releases. I choose ReentrantLock when I need tryLock with a timeout, interruptible waits, fairness or several conditions. Rules: lock the smallest scope, always unlock in finally , never call alien code while holding a lock, and use a global lock order or timeouts to avoid deadlock.

title: ConcurrentHashMap check-then-act
text: Find the bug and fix it. A word-count service uses a ConcurrentHashMap and still produces wrong counts under load expected 100,000, observed 96,000-99,000 varying per run . The author says "it is a concurrent map, so it is thread-safe". Map<String, Integer counts = new ConcurrentHashMap< ; void add String w { if !counts.containsKey w counts.put w, 0 ; counts.put w, counts.get w + 1 ; }

title: Double booking
text: Explain the race, fix it, and say whether a global lock is acceptable. A seat-booking class for a theatre with 200 seats. During a launch with 3,000 concurrent users, 14 seats were sold twice. The code: Seat s = show.findFree category ; if s != null { s.setTaken true ; return new Ticket s ; } return null; The author wants one global synchronized method. The booking API averages 400 requests/s at peak; each booking takes about 1 ms of CPU.

title: Deadlock
text: Explain and fix it. A wallet service transfers money between accounts. Under load the thread dump shows two threads blocked forever: "T1" waiting to lock <0x7f1 Account B , holding <0x7e0 Account A "T2" waiting to lock <0x7e0 Account A , holding <0x7f1 Account B Found one Java-level deadlock. void transfer Account from, Account to, long amt { synchronized from { synchronized to { from.debit amt ; to.credit amt ; } } } Both transfer A,B and transfer B,A run concurrently.

title: Atomics and CAS
text: How does compare-and-swap work, when do you choose atomics over locks, and what are their limits? CAS sets a variable to a new value only if it still holds the expected old value, as one atomic hardware step. Atomics AtomicInteger , AtomicBoolean , AtomicReference protect one variable lock-free, great for counters and "claim" flags. Limits: they cover one variable only, so two related fields need a lock or one AtomicReference to an immutable holder; heavy contention burns CPU in retries; and the ABA problem exists.

title: Atomics limits
text: Why is it wrong despite using atomics, and how do you fix it? A rate limiter allows 100 requests per second per user. A load test with 16 threads shows up to 140 requests per second admitted at window boundaries. The code: AtomicInteger count = new AtomicInteger ; AtomicLong windowStart = new AtomicLong System.currentTimeMillis ; boolean allow { long now = System.currentTimeMillis ; if now - windowStart.get = 1000 { windowStart.set now ; count.set 0 ; } return count.incrementAndGet <= 100; }

title: Testing concurrency
text: What is wrong with both tests and how do you rewrite them? A teammate's test for the parking lot passes locally and fails 1 in 20 on CI: @Test void feeIsThreeHours throws Exception { Ticket t = lot.park CAR ; Thread.sleep 3 60 60 1000 ; // CI timeout after 10 min assertEquals 120, lot.unpark t .rupees ; } @Test void parksConcurrently { new Thread - lot.park CAR .start ; new Thread - lot.park CAR .start ; assertEquals 2, lot.occupied ; }

title: Executors
text: Why does it die and what is the correct design? A thumbnail service accepts 800 jobs/s and processes 300/s using Executors.newFixedThreadPool 8 . After 20 minutes pods restart with OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space . Heap histogram: num instances bytes class name 1: 2,400,000 1,150,000,000 com.acme.ThumbnailJob 2: 2,400,000 230,400,000 java.util.concurrent.LinkedBlockingQueue$Node CPU is at 100% on 8 cores; GC time is rising.

title: Java rulebook for LLD
text: Which Java habits make an LLD answer look senior? Pick the five you would never skip and justify them. Immutability by default final , records, List.copyOf , constructor injection against interfaces, fail fast with Optional instead of null , money as BigDecimal or integer minor units and time via java.time with an injected Clock , and documented thread-safety. Also equals/hashCode together for map keys, and never swallowing InterruptedException .

title: God class
text: Show the new classes, the patterns you actually use, and the order of the refactor. You inherit a 600-line ParkingLot with 25 methods: spot search, fee calculation, ticket persistence to a file, SMS sending, and printing. A concurrency fix needs one lock, but unrelated features keep colliding in merges and the single lock blocks SMS sending and parking together. Tests need a real file and a real SMS stub.

title: Code review of a snippet
text: List the problems in priority order and show the corrected core. You review a candidate's wallet snippet. Production stakes: money, multiple threads. public class Wallet { public double balance; public static Map<String, Wallet all = new HashMap< ; public Wallet get String id { return all.get id ; } // null when missing public void pay double amt { try { Thread.sleep 10 ; } catch InterruptedException e {} balance -= amt; } public String today { return new SimpleDateFormat "yyyy-MM-dd" .format new Date ; } }

title: What an Adapter is
text: What is the Adapter pattern, and what problem does it solve? Give a real example from the JDK or Android.
